a425.speaker: António Monteiro, UCID member of parliament (Cape Verde)
a425.name: António Monteiro
a425.title: UCID member of parliament (Cape Verde)
a425.speech: Speaking at the party headquarters in São Vicente, spoke of the lack of investment to increase the injection of renewables into the grid: "First of all, the fuel distribution company must use cheaper fuels. We have Porto Novo and Fogo, which ought to be using fuel 180 and unfortunately are not using it for logistical reasons. UCID asks the government to carry out quickly the auctions that would allow more renewable energy in the country and for this energy to be injected into the grid so that the final consumer, both families and companies, can have access to much more acceptable energy costs than those at present."

a425.speaker: António Monteiro, UCID member of parliament (Cape Verde)
a425.name: António Monteiro
a425.title: UCID member of parliament (Cape Verde)
a425.speech: Argued that the country should take advantage of all available mechanisms to invest and reduce the price of electricity, suggesting recourse to the funds of the Climate and Environment Fund and of the third Millennium Challenge Corporation Compact: "The question that arises is that we have to take advantage of all the opportunities the country may have available. But, unfortunately, what we have is that, since 2010-2011, and we are in 2024, for 13 years we have had no significant investment in the matter of improving renewable energy in Cape Verde. This is unacceptable, and hence we have some of the highest energy costs in the world at this moment."

a425.speaker: António Monteiro, UCID member of parliament (Cape Verde)
a425.name: António Monteiro
a425.title: UCID member of parliament (Cape Verde)
a425.speech: "The increase in energy in Cape Verde has a highly negative impact on taxpayers' pockets and ends up removing the competitiveness of Cape Verdean companies and of the country, and negatively impacts citizens' day-to-day lives. And this electricity increase means that, instead of continuing to have inflation falling, with this increase the trend of rising inflation increases considerably."

a425.speaker: UCID (party position)
a425.name: UCID (party position)
a425.speech: The party recalls that having more expensive energy negatively impacts the lives of Cape Verdeans and takes away competitiveness from companies; advocates combating the losses which, between January and September of last year, represented a quarter of the energy produced by Electra nationally, and considers it necessary to prevent part of that loss from being introduced into the tariff charged to consumers.

a443.speaker: Ecole Internationale de Graphisme (EIG Benin) (press statement)
a443.name: Ecole Internationale de Graphisme (EIG Benin) (press statement)
a443.speech: "Today, we are proud to announce the renewal of our partnership, marking a new phase of growth and opportunities for our students," and set out the commitments of the strategic partnership with IFRI-UAC: to strengthen training programmes, develop innovative projects and solutions in computing, electronics and digital technology, co-create certifying courses co-signed by the two institutions, offer design and graphics training to IFRI students, and provide immersion internships in EIG's studios ; thanked "Professor Eugene C. EZIN, Director of IFRI-UAC, for his commitment and constant support for this collaboration" ; "In renewing our commitment with IFRI, we affirm our desire to contribute actively to the evolution of education and training in Africa."

a476.speaker: Harmonize, Tanzanian musician and owner of Konde Music Worldwide
a476.name: Harmonize
a476.title: Tanzanian musician and owner of Konde Music Worldwide
a476.speech: Came out and said there was no need to go to the National Arts Council (Basata) for arbitration over an artist whom he himself had brought out, and that he therefore wishes Ibraah all the best.

a520.speaker: Julius Debrah, Chief of Staff (Ghana)
a520.name: Julius Debrah
a520.title: Chief of Staff (Ghana)
a520.speech: Has annulled all appointments and recruitments made into the Public Services after December 7, 2024; according to the Chief of Staff, the appointments did not comply with established good governance practices and principles.

a520.speaker: Office of the Chief of Staff (letter/statement to heads of government institutions)
a520.name: Office of the Chief of Staff (letter/statement to heads of government institutions)
a520.speech: Instructed all heads of government institutions to take immediate steps to nullify such appointments and recruitments and submit a comprehensive report on the actions taken by February 17, 2025.

a832.speaker: Mwinyi Zahera, technical director of Namungo and former colleague of Al-Hilal coach Florent Ibenge at the DR Congo national team
a832.name: Mwinyi Zahera
a832.title: technical director of Namungo and former colleague of Al-Hilal coach Florent Ibenge at the DR Congo national team
a832.speech: Gave advice to Yanga ahead of the match, telling them to be very careful in building their attacks and stressing that if they fail to be careful they could face surprise counter-attacks from Al-Hilal, as happened in the last match between the two teams: “Yanga need to concentrate more on protecting themselves and not allowing Al-Hilal’s quick attacks. These are the champions of Sudan, and often when they play away from home they can be very dangerous on surprise attacks” ; “Ibenge is an expert at using surprise tactics and changing quickly. Yanga need to have discipline and concentration for all the minutes of the match. This will help them avoid the sudden attacks that Al-Hilal can use at any time”; urged Yanga to play with discipline and not to lose the ball easily in dangerous areas.

a1503.speaker: Department of Agriculture, Land Reform and Rural Development of South Africa (announcement)
a1503.name: Department of Agriculture
a1503.title: Land Reform and Rural Development of South Africa (announcement)
a1503.speech: announced last week that members of the public will be able to apply to lease 700 000 hectares of underutilised or vacant state land in seven of the provinces.

a1503.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa (newsletter to the nation)
a1503.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1503.title: President of South Africa (newsletter to the nation)
a1503.speech: says state-owned agricultural land will soon be released for farming - a major milestone in the agrarian reform process. "Agricultural land is the mainstay of our natural resource base. The availability and sustainable use of farmland to grow crops and for animal husbandry is key to our very survival," he said. "South Africa has vast tracts of land suitable for agricultural production, with 37.9% of our total land area currently being used for commercial agriculture." ; "In my state of the nation address earlier this year I committed that state-owned agricultural land would soon be released for farming. This is a major milestone in the agrarian reform process, and gives effect to the promise of the Freedom Charter that the land shall be shared among those who work it," said Ramaphosa. "Our redistributive vision aims to strike a balance between social justice and redress, and enhancing agricultural output by bringing more black farmers into the mainstream of the economy."

a1503.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1503.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1503.title: President of South Africa
a1503.speech: On land dispossession and the 1913 Natives Land Act: "Given our history, broadening access to agricultural land for commercial production and subsistence farming is a national priority... Although the post-1994 land reform process has resulted in more land being restored and restituted to black South Africans, the pernicious effects of the 1913 Natives Land Act continue to be in patterns of farmland ownership." ; "By depriving our people of their right to own and work the land on which they depended for sustenance and livelihood, this great injustice effectively engineered the poverty of black South Africans... Its aim was to destroy our people's prospects for self-reliance, independence and economic prosperity. At the most fundamental of levels, it destroyed our ability to feed ourselves."

a1503.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1503.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1503.title: President of South Africa
a1503.speech: On land concentration and social unrest: "The continued monopolisation of a key means of production like land is not just an obstacle to advancing a more egalitarian society; it is also a recipe for social unrest... The hunger for land to farm is growing, especially among the rural poor. And for a number of reasons, the pace of land reform in this particular sector has been slow and unsatisfactory."

a1503.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, President of South Africa
a1503.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a1503.title: President of South Africa
a1503.speech: On the goal of the land release: "The ultimate goal of releasing these land parcels is to transform the agricultural landscape by growing a new generation of farmers... Leasing land under such favourable conditions must spur them to think big; to not just grow their own businesses but to advance shared wealth and prosperity in the communities in which they farm. They must heal the deep divisions of our past. They must dispel the stereotype that only white farmers are commercially successful in South Africa, and that black farmers are perpetually 'emerging.' In working this land; in turning it to productive use, they will indeed turn swords into ploughshares. They will become the faces of national reconciliation."

a1503.speaker: 2019 report of the Presidential Advisory Panel on Land Reform and Agriculture
a1503.name: 2019 report of the Presidential Advisory Panel on Land Reform and Agriculture
a1503.speech: According to the report, cited by Ramaphosa, "while we export food, back home, 41% of people in rural areas and 59.4% in urban areas have severely inadequate access to food."

a1571.speaker: Assa Badiallo Touré, Colonel-Major (physician), Malian Minister of Health and Social Development
a1571.name: Assa Badiallo Touré
a1571.title: Colonel-Major (physician), Malian Minister of Health and Social Development
a1571.speech: Stressed that "The SanDi project fits fully within the implementation of the national digital health strategy (2024-2028), the national rural electrification policy, and the Sustainable Development Goals."

a1571.speaker: Dr. Itama Mayikuli Christian, Representative of the WHO Office in Mali
a1571.name: Dr. Itama Mayikuli Christian
a1571.title: Representative of the WHO Office in Mali
a1571.speech: According to him, the activities planned under the EMU project include: establishing a cohort of 80 health professionals trained and ready to be mobilized within 72 hours in the event of an emergency; developing standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the activation, mobilization and deployment of the Emergency Medical Teams; and conducting simulation exercises to test preparedness for epidemics and public health emergencies.

a1721.speaker: Dr Sié Kambou, specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.name: Dr Sié Kambou
a1721.title: specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.speech: On what biotechnology is: "There is no single typical definition of biotechnology. When you ferment dolo, that is biotechnology, because living organisms are used to produce alcohol. Likewise, when soumbala is fermented, that too is biotechnology. Biotechnology strongly involves living organisms; we oblige them to produce what we need. We can therefore say that biotechnology, or the genetic modification of products, is the use of the properties of organisms to produce goods and services for the benefit of humanity."

a1721.speaker: Dr Sié Kambou, specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.name: Dr Sié Kambou
a1721.title: specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.speech: On grafting and cloning: "Grafting consists of implanting into the tissues a fragment taken from another plant or from the same plant so that it continues to grow, becoming one with the first. And since grafting answers the question of how to produce several identical copies of a given variety, we would say that grafting is also cloning, since what is produced are identical copies of the desired tree."

a1721.speaker: Dr Sié Kambou, specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.name: Dr Sié Kambou
a1721.title: specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.speech: On what genetically modified crops are: "You have to know that the genetically modified exists in nature. In reality, there exists in nature a bacterium called Basileus turgescent (Bt) which infects plants and injects certain genes into them to force them to produce proteins it feeds on. In nature, things are determined by genes. Eye colour, skin colour, height... are the work of genes. And it is this logic that researchers follow in their work. It is not an invention of the mind. ... forcing the plant to produce what we need is not a bad thing. For example, in medicine we force certain organisms to produce penicillin for man." ; "There is no problem and you have your wall. That is what GMOs are, the cultivation of genetically modified products."

a1721.speaker: Dr Sié Kambou, specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.name: Dr Sié Kambou
a1721.title: specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.speech: On Bt cotton: "I would rather refer you to INERA, which has worked a great deal on this. However, it should be noted that Bt cotton uses fewer pesticides and that is economically profitable for our cotton growers. The difference between Bt cotton and local cotton lies in the length of the fibres. Several treatments have to be carried out for Bt cotton and that is what the industrial processors deplore, because it costs them dearly. As a researcher, one could therefore continue the research to understand why these fibres are shorter, and so on until we obtain what we want."

a1721.speaker: Dr Sié Kambou, specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.name: Dr Sié Kambou
a1721.title: specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.speech: On why people are wary of GM products: "The United States was the first to work on GMOs, and public opinion does not make an issue of it. Soya and maize are grown over thousands of hectares and that poses no problem for Americans. The problem is at the level of the Europeans, but that does not stop them from continuing to work on GMOs, because they know that the genetically modified exists in nature through Basileus turgescente (Bt). The messaging about rejecting the consumption of GMO products is the work of agitators. Otherwise, how can one understand wanting to deny what exists in nature? Nowadays more than 60% of soya is produced from GMO soya; no one makes an issue of it and it is consumed everywhere. I therefore say it is good that there are people who are 'against' so that those who are 'for' take precautions to respect ethics."

a1721.speaker: Dr Sié Kambou, specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.name: Dr Sié Kambou
a1721.title: specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.speech: On biotechnology and environmental protection: "GMOs can allow us to have plants that resist pesticides, and free us from their use. Is that not better than drenching the environment with herbicides and the like? And that is the importance of GMOs for protecting the environment. The quantity of pesticides that enter Burkina Faso each year constitutes a public danger because you break a food chain. Herbicides destroy the plants insects feed on; the insects that eat these plants die; the birds that eat these insects will also die, as will the other animals that eat those birds, and afterwards the villager will pick up that dead animal and consume it in turn. If we weigh the pros and cons, explaining clearly what GMOs are and what pesticides contribute, I believe the population will prefer to consume GMOs."

a1721.speaker: Dr Sié Kambou, specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.name: Dr Sié Kambou
a1721.title: specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.speech: On whether fear of risk justifies rejecting GM crops: "The rejection of genetically modified crops can only be explained by two reasons: ethics, and dependence on large firms or companies for obtaining seed supply. ... GMOs make it possible to overcome natural barriers. ... Human beings, out of caution, are afraid of what is new, like Louis Pasteur at the discovery of the rabies serum. But when the success of the serum was seen, it spread and it is still used today. It is normal to be a little afraid of what one is not used to, but that does not justify stopping work on it. And progress cannot be stopped. Whether we like it or not, we cannot stop producing GMOs today; it will even expand, because GMOs render us enormous services. Now it is good that the researcher takes precautions and that poor countries get up to date with the technology. We have men capable of working on GMOs, they simply need to be equipped. And the proof: when MONSANTO came, it worked with Burkinabè. They worked well, because they are very well trained."

a1721.speaker: Dr Sié Kambou, specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.name: Dr Sié Kambou
a1721.title: specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.speech: On Monsanto: "Monsanto does not have too many problems with GMOs; it has far more problems with herbicides such as gluconate. Monsanto does not work only on GMOs. I have not yet seen an article implicating the use of GMOs as harmful to man. There is no scientific writing that proves it."

a1721.speaker: Dr Sié Kambou, specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.name: Dr Sié Kambou
a1721.title: specialist in plant biology and ecology, head of the applied research division at the National Forest Seed Centre (CNSF)
a1721.speech: On the stance Burkina Faso should take: "The advantage we have in Burkina is undeniable. We are one of the few countries in Africa to have a national biosafety agency that makes it possible to control everything connected with modified organisms. As a Burkinabè, as a human being, the researcher is not prepared to make available to others a product that is not good. The researcher has a moral duty not to make available to the population products whose consumption is harmful to their health. Organic consumption is a matter of fashion which does not necessarily mean anti-GMO, but rather anti-pesticide, and GMO products are also on that trajectory. For me, progress cannot be stopped; we have more to gain from supporting progress and from having equipment and laboratories that can be at the cutting edge of this new technology which, if used wisely, is very useful for ourselves."

a1779.speaker: Ibrahim Elmi Mohamed, Secretary General of the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Fisheries Resources (MAEPE-RH), Djibouti
a1779.name: Ibrahim Elmi Mohamed
a1779.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Fisheries Resources (MAEPE-RH), Djibouti
a1779.speech: "The creation of an information platform on water and sanitation is more than indispensable." ; Said that eradicating thirst and ensuring easy access to drinking water and sanitation are among the government's absolute priorities, notably for the MAEPE-RH; that the absence of tools that make use of these data heightens the sector's difficulties; that it is in this precise framework that the MAEPE-RH, through the Rural Hydraulics Directorate (DHR), took the initiative of establishing the national protocol for the monitoring and evaluation system for the WASH sector in rural areas with the financial support of USAID through UNICEF; that the consultancy began in September 2018 with the firm "Cosinus", selected to put this tool in place; that during the drafting phase the DHR involved all the sector's stakeholders and the information collected served as a reference in formulating the protocol's main pillars; and that "It is indispensable for us that the WASH sector take a qualitative look at this document in order to share their expertise during the three days of the workshop."

a1832.speaker: EDF 2024 Integrated Annual Report
a1832.name: EDF 2024 Integrated Annual Report
a1832.speech: Shows the fund's net profit rose to K18.9 billion from K9.7 billion the previous year while its total assets grew to K115.7 billion from K95.1 billion in 2023.

a1832.speaker: Export Development Fund (EDF)
a1832.name: Export Development Fund (EDF)
a1832.speech: Said its investment strategy aligns with national priorities under Malawi 2063, focusing on sectors with clear economic and social value.

a1832.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, economist
a1832.name: Velli Nyirongo
a1832.title: economist
a1832.speech: Said in an interview that EDF plays a catalytic role in easing financing constraints, but its impact on SME-led industrialisation and export diversification remains limited in scope: "Many beneficiaries are concentrated in urban centres, while rural-based and informal SMEs, particularly women- and youth-led enterprises—remain underserved."

a1832.speaker: Hastings Thondolo, Mach Milk Company factory manager
a1832.name: Hastings Thondolo
a1832.title: Mach Milk Company factory manager
a1832.speech: Said limited access to capital hinders his firm's ability to fulfil large-scale contracts: "At the moment, we are supplying some local shops in Blantyre, but we do not have the finances required to finance a long-term contract demanded by major retail chains such as Chipiku and Shoprite."

a1832.speaker: Hastings Thondolo, Mach Milk Company factory manager
a1832.name: Hastings Thondolo
a1832.title: Mach Milk Company factory manager
a1832.speech: Said the absence of publicly available impact data makes it difficult to assess how EDF financing translates into exports or industrial transformation.

a1887.speaker: The two Heads of State (Abdulfatah Al-Sissi of Egypt and Ismail Omar Guelleh of Djibouti), joint communiqué
a1887.name: The two Heads of State (Abdulfatah Al-Sissi of Egypt and Ismail Omar Guelleh of Djibouti)
a1887.title: joint communiqué
a1887.speech: Welcomed their common desire to further tighten their strategic relationship and committed to deploying more efforts to develop bilateral cooperation by revitalising the mechanisms of joint work, notably within the framework of the 4th joint ministerial commission held in Cairo in January 2010, as well as political consultation ; also underlined the need to explore new horizons in order to raise their fraternal relations to the highest level in all fields, such as strengthening trade exchanges, economic cooperation, the creation of the Egyptian logistics zone, inter-port cooperation, education, higher education, health (notably through the project to create an Egyptian hospital in Djibouti in collaboration with the ministry of health), capacity building, fishing and fishery resources, energy, petroleum, natural gas, housing, road construction, tourism, banks, and the fight against terrorism and extremism.

a1887.speaker: Ismail Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti
a1887.name: Ismail Omar Guelleh
a1887.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti
a1887.speech: Expressed his appreciation for the achievements recorded and the efforts made, under the enlightened vision of President Al-Sissi, to promote economic development and ensure the security and stability of Egypt.

a1887.speaker: Government of Djibouti
a1887.name: Government of Djibouti
a1887.speech: Expressed its keen thanks for the donation of equipment, medical supplies, foodstuffs and equipment for people with special needs that the Egyptian government, in a surge of fraternal solidarity, offered to the Djiboutian people to confront the coronavirus pandemic.

a1887.speaker: The two parties (Djibouti and Egypt), joint communiqué
a1887.name: The two parties (Djibouti and Egypt)
a1887.title: joint communiqué
a1887.speech: Reaffirmed the importance of establishing better consultation between the countries bordering the Red Sea, in order to strengthen the security and stability of the region, a strategic route for maritime traffic and international trade, through joint mechanisms.

a1887.speaker: The two parties (Djibouti and Egypt), joint communiqué
a1887.name: The two parties (Djibouti and Egypt)
a1887.title: joint communiqué
a1887.speech: Agreed that the Nile must constitute a means of cooperation allowing the development objectives of Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia to be achieved, and reaffirmed the necessity of resuming negotiations on the Renaissance Dam in order to reach an agreement that can preserve the interests of the three countries, prevent any damage and support efforts for prosperity and stability throughout the region.

a1887.speaker: Ismail Omar Guelleh, President of the Republic of Djibouti
a1887.name: Ismail Omar Guelleh
a1887.title: President of the Republic of Djibouti
a1887.speech: Concerning the Palestinian question, welcomed the success of the Egyptian ceasefire initiative which made it possible to end the Israeli aggression and save the lives of "our Palestinian brothers".

a1887.speaker: The two parties (Djibouti and Egypt), joint communiqué
a1887.name: The two parties (Djibouti and Egypt)
a1887.title: joint communiqué
a1887.speech: Underlined the need to pursue efforts to reach a comprehensive and permanent outcome based on the two-state solution allowing Palestine to return to the June 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as Capital, in accordance with the Arab initiative and international resolutions.

a1887.speaker: Abdulfatah Al-Sissi, President of the Arab Republic of Egypt
a1887.name: Abdulfatah Al-Sissi
a1887.title: President of the Arab Republic of Egypt
a1887.speech: Wished to thank his Djiboutian counterpart, H.E. Ismail Omar Guelleh, for the warm welcome and generous hospitality which his delegation and he himself received, and in turn invited him to make a visit to Egypt.

a1887.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Djibouti (communiqué)
a1887.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Djibouti (communiqué)
a1887.speech: Communiqué of the ministry of foreign affairs and international cooperation — the source document of this joint statement on the Egyptian President's visit to Djibouti.

a1941.speaker: Sofia Murangi, educator and caregiver in Kavango West
a1941.name: Sofia Murangi
a1941.title: educator and caregiver in Kavango West
a1941.speech: "I couldn't bear to see the conditions these children were living in. Their field had not produced crops in years, leaving them nothing to eat. It broke my heart as a mother, so I opened my home to them."

a1941.speaker: Klara Kakororo, Reach Namibia's Orphans and Vulnerable Children technical director
a1941.name: Klara Kakororo
a1941.title: Reach Namibia's Orphans and Vulnerable Children technical director
a1941.speech: "Without the guidance and support of parents, these young heads of families often struggle to meet basic needs like food, education and healthcare." ; "The emotional burden of losing their childhood to these responsibilities leaves them isolated, stressed and vulnerable to exploitation. This cycle not only jeopardizes their future, but also has a ripple-effect on the wider community, threatening the long-term social and economic stability of the region."

a1941.speaker: Mariane's class teacher, Simanya Combined School
a1941.name: Mariane's class teacher
a1941.title: Simanya Combined School
a1941.speech: "In the first week of school, she has made friends, and her classmates have been very welcoming." ; "However, we're also mindful of the circumstances that brought the girls here, so we ensure that the life skills teacher continuously assesses their academic and psycho-social development."

a2207.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a2207.name: John Dramani Mahama
a2207.title: President of Ghana
a2207.speech: Outlined plans to reshape Ghana's economy through a 24-hour economy policy, stressing the need for a shift in the country's economic approach and arguing that round-the-clock productivity is key to reversing years of stagnation: "The era of an economy that sleeps at night must end. Ghana needs continuous productivity, more jobs, and a stronger export base. The 24-hour economy is not just a policy, it is a necessity." ; explained that under this initiative, businesses will be encouraged to operate throughout the day and night, and the government will work to provide stable electricity, improved security, and better transport systems to support night-time production and trade.

a2207.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a2207.name: John Dramani Mahama
a2207.title: President of Ghana
a2207.speech: Spoke about his $10 billion 'Big Push' infrastructure plan, which he said would expand roads, railways, and energy systems while creating thousands of jobs: "This is a bold step towards building a Ghana that stands on its own industries and workforce instead of continuously seeking foreign assistance."

a2207.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a2207.name: John Dramani Mahama
a2207.title: President of Ghana
a2207.speech: Stressed the role of agriculture in reducing import dependence, pointing to the Agriculture for Economic Transformation Agenda, which seeks to strengthen local food production and cut Ghana's $2 billion annual food import bill; said initiatives such as the Feed Ghana Programme and the Farm-to-Table Poultry Initiative would give farmers access to land, mechanised farming tools, and inputs while promoting large-scale food processing to help stabilise prices. "Our future prosperity depends on our ability to feed ourselves, produce what we consume, and export more than we import. That is the foundation of true economic independence."

a2207.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a2207.name: John Dramani Mahama
a2207.title: President of Ghana
a2207.speech: Urged Ghanaians to support policies aimed at reducing dependence on donor aid, IMF bailouts, and excessive imports, insisting that the path to economic stability lies in productivity, innovation, and disciplined governance.

a2228.speaker: Council of Ministers of Djibouti, chaired by President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh (official record of the 20th session)
a2228.name: Council of Ministers of Djibouti
a2228.title: chaired by President Ismaïl Omar Guelleh (official record of the 20th session)
a2228.speech: Examined and approved the following texts: draft laws approving the financial accounts for the 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023 financial years of the National Food Analysis Laboratory (LANAA); a draft order adopting the LANAA's 2025 provisional budget; a draft law approving the financial accounts of the Djiboutian Roads Agency (ADR) for 2023; a draft order approving the ADR's 2025 provisional budget; a draft order approving the 2025 provisional budget of the Djibouti Economic Development Fund (FDED); a draft order approving the 2025 provisional budget of the Military Retirement Fund (CMR); a draft order approving the 2025 provisional budget of the Central Purchasing Body for Essential Medicines and Materials (CAMME); and a draft order approving the 2025 provisional budget of the International Hydrocarbons Company of Djibouti (SIHD). The Council also cleared and approved the LANAA's financial accounts for the earlier 2020 to 2022 financial years.

a2228.speaker: Minister of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries, Livestock and Marine Resources
a2228.name: Minister of Agriculture
a2228.title: Water, Fisheries, Livestock and Marine Resources
a2228.speech: Gave a report on his participation in the "COP 16 - UNCCD" Conference held under the theme "Our land. Our Future" from 2 to 13 December 2024 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

a2228.speaker: Minister of Youth and Culture
a2228.name: Minister of Youth and Culture
a2228.speech: Gave a report on her participation in the 19th Session of the Intergovernmental Committee for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage from 2 to 7 December 2024 in Asunción, Paraguay, during which she took part in the ceremony celebrating the inscription of the Xeer Issa on the representative list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

a2228.speaker: Minister of Youth and Culture
a2228.name: Minister of Youth and Culture
a2228.speech: Made a communication on the holding of a Colloquium on the Developments and Prospects of Djiboutian Archives (EPAD'24), to be held on 18 and 19 December 2024 at the headquarters of the National Archives (ANPC) under the theme "State of Djiboutian archives: assessment, challenges and prospects," thirteen years after the first event entitled "History and archives" organised in 2011.

a2261.speaker: World Bank, 2025 report on the assessment of policies and institutions in Africa (CPIA)
a2261.name: World Bank
a2261.title: 2025 report on the assessment of policies and institutions in Africa (CPIA)
a2261.speech: Sounds the alarm that 53% of sub-Saharan African countries are now classified as at high risk of debt distress or already in debt distress, against only 25% in 2012, a figure that even reached 61% at the height of the crisis in 2021 ; According to the report, Benin ranks first with a score of 4.5 on debt policy and management alongside Côte d'Ivoire and ahead of all other countries.

a2261.speaker: World Bank report
a2261.name: World Bank report
a2261.speech: Also insists on transparency in debt management as a lever of performance, noting that certain countries such as Togo, Burundi and Cameroon have recently adopted ambitious reforms to better regulate the debt of public enterprises by imposing publication obligations or debt ceilings ; Highlights the rise of multilateral institutions as a source of development financing, with net multilateral debt flows to IDA-eligible countries rising from 6 to 20 billion dollars between 2012 and 2023, while bilateral and private creditors have largely reduced their exposure in the region.

a2261.speaker: World Bank
a2261.name: World Bank
a2261.speech: For the World Bank, recent efforts on fiscal consolidation and restructuring are encouraging, but insufficient in the medium term: pressures remain strong -- heavy bond maturities, contraction of foreign aid, rate volatility.

a2306.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2306.name: Donald Trump
a2306.title: US President
a2306.speech: hailed Africa's exceptional economic potential and called for building win-win partnerships based on trade and investment rather than on aid ; also stressed the need for peace as a prerequisite for any development, announcing an expanded US-Africa summit in the autumn to deepen these exchanges.

a2525.speaker: Right to Information Commission (RTIC)
a2525.name: Right to Information Commission (RTIC)
a2525.speech: has formally requested a response from the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) regarding its refusal to release information on alleged tax evasion and money laundering cases involving certain companies ; The Commission emphasised that public institutions must assist in investigations and warned that failure to comply would not hinder its review process ; the RTIC has advised all parties to refrain from making prejudicial public statements while investigations continue.

a2525.speaker: Joseph Bediako, Convener of the Movement for Truth and Accountability (petition)
a2525.name: Joseph Bediako
a2525.title: Convener of the Movement for Truth and Accountability (petition)
a2525.speech: accused the FIC of failing to provide requested details, having initially sought information in December 2024, followed by a reminder in January 2025, and after receiving no response escalated the matter to the RTIC; the requested information includes the status of investigations initiated since 2020, any findings or conclusions, and any other relevant details.

a2525.speaker: Yaw Sarpong Boateng, Executive Secretary of RTIC
a2525.name: Yaw Sarpong Boateng
a2525.title: Executive Secretary of RTIC
a2525.speech: Citing Sections 43(2)(b) and 70 of the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989), has directed the FIC to justify its refusal and provide the requested details within seven days.

a2525.speaker: Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA)
a2525.name: Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA)
a2525.speech: has responded to Joseph Bediako's request, providing data on audits, penalties and referrals to the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO): the figures indicate that from 2021 to 2024, a total of 548 importers were audited, leading to assessed liabilities exceeding GH¢1 billion, and 537 cases were referred to EOCO for further action; the GRA also outlined penalties imposed on importers who under declared customs values.

a2542.speaker: Goni Umar Farouk, Chairman of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), Kano State chapter
a2542.name: Goni Umar Farouk
a2542.title: Chairman of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), Kano State chapter
a2542.speech: On the participation of minors in the #EndBadGovernance protest and their arrest: "Well, it is unfortunate that it happened, but you know, the minors were not perhaps even aware of why the protest was taking place. They may have just joined the processions. On days of celebrations like Eid and Christmas, you'd see them just following any march. When the emirs go to the praying ground, they just follow. So it is unfortunate that anytime we have protests, everybody on the street would just follow."

a2542.speaker: Goni Umar Farouk, Chairman of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), Kano State chapter
a2542.name: Goni Umar Farouk
a2542.title: Chairman of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), Kano State chapter
a2542.speech: On how the episode portrays northern Nigeria: "The issue of the image of the North should not be linked to this situation. You know we have been talking about the out-of-school children, so this is not something new. We have millions of children who are not in school, who are not employed, whose parents do not even know where they are, what they are doing and where they are living. So, it is not the protest that has shown the North to be having problems. It is a problem that has been with us for many years. Unless parents look after their children, give them moral upbringing and training, send them to school, this kind of situation will continue."

a2542.speaker: Goni Umar Farouk, Chairman of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), Kano State chapter
a2542.name: Goni Umar Farouk
a2542.title: Chairman of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), Kano State chapter
a2542.speech: On the role of parents and society: "Parents have a role to play but you see, when they are not employed and they do not have any means of livelihood, this affects their children. To stop this kind of situation, first of all, before you come to the government, parents must make sure that they have the number of children they can take care of. They should be with them; they should not send them out to beg. They should not send them far away for Qur'anic education, where they would end up begging on the streets and whenever there is any protest or riot they just join. Look at what happened when the NCC digital innovation park was looted and the children were there."

a2542.speaker: Goni Umar Farouk, Chairman of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), Kano State chapter
a2542.name: Goni Umar Farouk
a2542.title: Chairman of the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF), Kano State chapter
a2542.speech: On the way forward: "Government must make sure they remove the underage children from the streets. Once they are on the streets, it (protest) would continue to happen. So, government has a role. Maybe the state assembly should enact a legislation that would stop children from roaming about, and you know, if you are to ask these children who were arrested, their states of origin, you will find that most of them are not from Kano. The government, I learnt, has started a census for foreigners, but it should also conduct census of people roaming the street, who perhaps, are not even indigenes of the state and ask them why they are here; what profession or trade they are into. If they don't have any, the government must find a way of addressing the problem."

a2772.speaker: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a2772.name: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
a2772.speech: Announced on Thursday that it will cancel the Africa Hometown scheme, after an episode that experts say illustrates the potential impact of fake news and populist narratives to shape migration policy.

a2772.speaker: Experts
a2772.name: Experts
a2772.speech: Say the episode illustrates the potential impact of fake news and populist narratives to shape migration policy.

a2772.speaker: Nigerian government (statement)
a2772.name: Nigerian government (statement)
a2772.speech: An erroneous Nigerian government statement about a "special visa category" helped spur false claims online.

a2772.speaker: Critics of Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba (on social media)
a2772.name: Critics of Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba (on social media)
a2772.speech: Accused him on social media of plotting to bring "millions of Africans and Kurds" into Japan.

a2772.speaker: Elon Musk, US-based billionaire owner of X
a2772.name: Elon Musk
a2772.title: US-based billionaire owner of X
a2772.speech: Commenting on the claims regarding the Japanese scheme, he wrote: "If this continues, there will be no Japan, just some islands where Japanese people used to live."

a2772.speaker: Akihiko Tanaka, JICA President
a2772.name: Akihiko Tanaka
a2772.title: JICA President
a2772.speech: Said the backlash had overwhelmed participating municipalities. "Reactions spread based on misunderstandings and confusion," he told reporters in Tokyo. "The Africa Hometown initiative will be withdrawn."

a2772.speaker: Akihiko Tanaka, JICA President
a2772.name: Akihiko Tanaka
a2772.title: JICA President
a2772.speech: Stressed that JICA will continue international exchange efforts, including with African partners, but underlined that the agency "does not deal with immigration issues".

a2772.speaker: Local media
a2772.name: Local media
a2772.speech: Reported that one city fielded as many as 200 angry calls a day.

a2872.speaker: Antonio Costa, President of the European Council
a2872.name: Antonio Costa
a2872.title: President of the European Council
a2872.speech: Argues that the European Union must not remain impassive about the humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip and said he believes in dialogue with Israel for a ceasefire; said the European Union cannot remain indifferent to the situation in the Gaza Strip. “We must not be impassive and we must engage in dialogue with Israel and seek to have Israel do what it has to do: accept the ceasefire, allow humanitarian aid to reach the population of Gaza” (quoted by Lusa) ; called the situation in Gaza unacceptable: “No one can ignore what we see on television and what we read in the press: the humanitarian situation in Gaza is completely unacceptable”

a2872.speaker: Antonio Costa, President of the European Council
a2872.name: Antonio Costa
a2872.title: President of the European Council
a2872.speech: Announced that the head of EU community diplomacy will assess the next steps regarding the association agreement between Brussels and Tel Aviv

a2987.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft co-founder
a2987.name: Bill Gates
a2987.title: Microsoft co-founder
a2987.speech: Announced Thursday an accelerated timeframe for giving away his fortune as he touted artificial intelligence as a game-changer to boost public health and save lives globally. ; "People will say a lot of things about me when I die, but I am determined that 'he died rich' will not be one of them," Gates wrote. ; Separate from the Gates Foundation, the Microsoft founder said he plans to continue to provide funding for initiatives to expand access to affordable energy and for breakthrough research into Alzheimer's disease.

a2987.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft co-founder
a2987.name: Bill Gates
a2987.title: Microsoft co-founder
a2987.speech: The Tesla CEO pushed through draconian cuts to the US Agency for International Development because Musk "didn't go to a party that weekend," Gates told the New York Times in an apparent dig at Musk's lifestyle. ; Gates called the cuts "stunning," far more severe than expected. ; Musk is "the one who cut the USAID budget," Gates told the New York Times. "He put it in the wood chipper." ; In an interview with the Financial Times, Gates ridiculed Musk's apparent confusion of Gaza Province in Mozambique with Gaza in the Middle East as the Trump administration targeted programs. ; "The picture of the world's richest man killing the world's poorest children is not a pretty one," Gates said of Musk in an interview with the Financial Times.

a2987.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft co-founder
a2987.name: Bill Gates
a2987.title: Microsoft co-founder
a2987.speech: In the blog post, Gates credited the writings of 19th-century US steel magnate Andrew Carnegie, whose foundation is still around. But Gates told the New York Times he had no designs on creating a "forever" foundation out of "some weird legacy thing," preferring to pump out billions more to take advantage of emerging technologies. ; "The tools are so phenomenal," he said of the potential for AI in global health. ; "All the intelligence will be in the AI, and so you will have a personal doctor that's as good as somebody who has a full-time dedicated doctor — that's actually better than even what rich countries have," Gates told the New York Times.

a2987.speaker: Bill Gates, Microsoft co-founder
a2987.name: Bill Gates
a2987.title: Microsoft co-founder
a2987.speech: While private foundations can do a lot, Gates described the government role as essential, ruing deep budget cuts by the United States, Britain, France and other countries. ; "It's unclear whether the world's richest countries will continue to stand up for its poorest people. But the one thing we can guarantee is that, in all of our work, the Gates Foundation will support efforts to help people and countries pull themselves out of poverty," he wrote.

a2987.speaker: Forbes "real-time" billionaire list
a2987.name: Forbes "real-time" billionaire list
a2987.speech: Gates is listed as the 13th on the Forbes "real-time" billionaire list, with a net worth of $112.6 billion. Musk is first with $383.2 billion.

a3108.speaker: United Nations official (anonymous)
a3108.name: United Nations official (anonymous)
a3108.speech: Told the BBC that hundreds of thousands of people are “slowly starving” in Kenyan refugee camps after US funding cuts reduced food rations to their lowest ever levels.

a3108.speaker: Medic at Kakuma’s Amusait Hospital (anonymous)
a3108.name: Medic at Kakuma’s Amusait Hospital (anonymous)
a3108.speech: Tells the BBC that the wrinkled, peeling skin and angry patches of red on the baby Hellen are the result of malnutrition.

a3108.speaker: Agnes Awila, refugee from northern Uganda
a3108.name: Agnes Awila
a3108.title: refugee from northern Uganda
a3108.speech: “The food is not enough, my children eat only once a day. If there’s no food what do you feed them?”

a3159.speaker: Adelino Muchanga, Chief Justice of the Republic of Mozambique
a3159.name: Adelino Muchanga
a3159.title: Chief Justice of the Republic of Mozambique
a3159.speech: Noted at the launch ceremony on February 22nd: “we want every Magistrate, each judicial officer and each judicial employee to be an agent of change, to be a defender of the rule of law… [and] we want to do our part and reiterate our commitment to protecting biodiversity, fighting corruption and protecting human rights and combating terrorism.”

a3159.speaker: Helen Pataki, USAID Mission Director
a3159.name: Helen Pataki
a3159.title: USAID Mission Director
a3159.speech: Emphasized commitment to the rule of law: “A strong justice sector is critical to improve the quality of life for all Mozambican citizens. JUSTA will work to improve coordination between justice sector institutions and promote a fair and efficient justice system. The United States stands with Mozambicans by strengthening public financial management, independent civil society and media, democratic processes and institutions, rule of law, and combating wildlife trafficking.”

a3171.speaker: Economists (unnamed)
a3171.name: Economists (unnamed)
a3171.speech: blame the inflation spike on excessive liquidity in circulation, a depreciating kwacha, and the country's chronic dependence on imports.

a3171.speaker: The International Economic Review (report)
a3171.name: The International Economic Review (report)
a3171.speech: painted a bleak picture this month: inflation has surpassed projections, forcing policymakers to reconsider short-term interventions.

a3171.speaker: Peter Mutharika, President of Malawi
a3171.name: Peter Mutharika
a3171.title: President of Malawi
a3171.speech: In his inaugural address, Mutharika vowed to "restore integrity and rebuild trust in state institutions."

a3171.speaker: Opposition parties and civic organizations
a3171.name: Opposition parties and civic organizations
a3171.speech: have urged caution, citing the need for immediate action on transparency, accountability, and judicial reform.

a3171.speaker: Analysts (unnamed)
a3171.name: Analysts (unnamed)
a3171.speech: argue that Mutharika's second coming could determine whether Malawi reclaims its democratic maturity or slides further into political fatigue.

a3171.speaker: Political insiders (anonymous)
a3171.name: Political insiders (anonymous)
a3171.speech: suggest that the Speaker's position has already become a hotbed of lobbying, with various factions eyeing the post as a strategic instrument for influence.

a3171.speaker: Government of Malawi (announcement)
a3171.name: Government of Malawi (announcement)
a3171.speech: announced that it will import 200,000 metric tons of maize from Zambia.

a3171.speaker: Agricultural experts
a3171.name: Agricultural experts
a3171.speech: warn that the move to import maize exposes deeper structural weaknesses.

a3171.speaker: Local media
a3171.name: Local media
a3171.speech: reported that smallholder farmers have been sidelined by delayed payments, inadequate inputs, and limited access to markets - issues that perpetuate dependency on imported grain.

a3171.speaker: Local media
a3171.name: Local media
a3171.speech: According to local media, the scaling back of donor support could translate into a 9% loss in government revenue this fiscal year - a blow that could stall development projects and social programs.

a3171.speaker: Public service workers, including teachers and healthcare professionals
a3171.name: Public service workers
a3171.title: including teachers and healthcare professionals
a3171.speech: fear that this funding gap could lead to delayed salaries and shortages of essential supplies.

a3171.speaker: Civil society groups
a3171.name: Civil society groups
a3171.speech: are already pressing the new administration to diversify Malawi's economic partnerships, strengthen domestic revenue collection, and prioritize spending efficiency.

a3368.speaker: 2023 Ghanaian government assessment (report)
a3368.name: 2023 Ghanaian government assessment (report)
a3368.speech: Highlighted the factory's reliance on obsolete technology as a primary reason for its closure.

a3368.speaker: Ralph Ayitey, National Treasurer of the Association of Ghana Industries
a3368.name: Ralph Ayitey
a3368.title: National Treasurer of the Association of Ghana Industries
a3368.speech: Noted that neighboring countries like Burkina Faso and Benin have thriving cotton sectors, while Ghana relies on imported cotton, burdened by a 5% duty that increases production costs.

a3368.speaker: Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia
a3368.name: Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia
a3368.speech: Proposed the "Buy Ghana First" policy, backed by law, which prioritizes local manufacturers for public and private procurement, allowing imports only when local supply is insufficient.

a3368.speaker: Sylvester Mensah, CEO of Ghana Eximbank, and Jerome Dunyo, Managing Director of Volta Star Textiles
a3368.name: Sylvester Mensah
a3368.title: CEO of Ghana Eximbank, and Jerome Dunyo, Managing Director of Volta Star Textiles
a3368.speech: Suggested that a public-private partnership model could attract private investment while maintaining public oversight.

a3368.speaker: Anti-Piracy Task Force
a3368.name: Anti-Piracy Task Force
a3368.speech: Advocated strengthening anti-smuggling measures and enforcing import controls to protect local manufacturers from counterfeit textiles.

a3368.speaker: Industry experts
a3368.name: Industry experts
a3368.speech: Suggested policies to regulate the quality of second-hand clothing imports, which would reduce waste and support local production.

a3402.speaker: Abdi Omar Nur ("Buraale"), displaced patient treated for a goiter
a3402.name: Abdi Omar Nur ("Buraale")
a3402.title: displaced patient treated for a goiter
a3402.speech: "I couldn't sleep or work because of the lump on my neck. Alhamdulillah, I received surgery. Now I can move my neck freely again."

a3402.speaker: Sahro Abdulle Ali, mother of seven and resident of Xaawo Taako camp treated for a lipoma
a3402.name: Sahro Abdulle Ali
a3402.title: mother of seven and resident of Xaawo Taako camp treated for a lipoma
a3402.speech: "After 12 years, now I feel that I can work again," Sahro told Kaab TV.

a3402.speaker: Fatima Ismail Warsame, chair of the Somali Women Health Professionals Council
a3402.name: Fatima Ismail Warsame
a3402.title: chair of the Somali Women Health Professionals Council
a3402.speech: "We are health volunteers. We collect reports on poor and displaced people in need of medical care. Then we appeal to hospitals and doctors. When approved, we help facilitate the treatment."

a3402.speaker: Dr. Hassan Omar Mursal, Director General of Germany Hospital
a3402.name: Dr. Hassan Omar Mursal
a3402.title: Director General of Germany Hospital
a3402.speech: "We don't set strict conditions. If the patient qualifies medically and surgery is feasible, we proceed."

a3415.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a3415.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a3415.title: Ukrainian President
a3415.speech: Said on Saturday that he wants the war in his country to end in 2025, stating that Ukraine "will do everything in its power" to end the war by diplomatic means over the coming year.

a3415.speaker: Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President
a3415.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
a3415.title: Ukrainian President
a3415.speech: Displayed a certain optimism after his telephone conversation with the future US president, saying he did not perceive in the Republican's remarks any intentions hostile to Ukrainian ambitions.

a3415.speaker: Frans Osinga, expert and former air force commander
a3415.name: Frans Osinga
a3415.title: expert and former air force commander
a3415.speech: Believes Zelensky's message was aimed at his citizens, his allies and also at Donald Trump: "Not only does Zelensky close no doors and thereby spare himself criticism from his people and his allies, but at the same time he is sending a message to Donald Trump: Ukraine cannot be kept out of the negotiations."

a3415.speaker: Frans Osinga, expert and former air force commander
a3415.name: Frans Osinga
a3415.title: expert and former air force commander
a3415.speech: Commented that the United States appears to be the only power capable of providing security guarantees to Ukraine: "Trump will therefore have to do the job."

a3415.speaker: Frans Osinga, expert and former air force commander
a3415.name: Frans Osinga
a3415.title: expert and former air force commander
a3415.speech: Stressed that a ceasefire would also be profitable for Russia, whose army is losing many soldiers, military equipment and armoured vehicles for each kilometre gained: "Russia risks facing serious problems if it persists in pursuing the fighting with the same intensity and if, at the same time, the West continues to support Ukraine. Putin therefore probably launched the offensive in the Donbass with the aim of conquering as much territory as possible and accumulating arguments before sitting down at the negotiating table to try to reach a truce."

a3415.speaker: Hans van Koningsbrugge, Russia expert
a3415.name: Hans van Koningsbrugge
a3415.title: Russia expert
a3415.speech: "Volodymyr Zelensky is confronted with a new political reality: the return of Donald Trump to the White House. This is not good news for Ukraine, at first sight, because of his desire to end the war quickly, but Donald Trump nevertheless has many assets." ; "It is not known, however, how far Kyiv and Moscow are prepared to cooperate. The outcome of the diplomatic track therefore remains unpredictable."

a3415.speaker: Fox News (US television channel)
a3415.name: Fox News (US television channel)
a3415.speech: Announced last Thursday that Donald Trump should "shortly" appoint a special representative for the Russian-Ukrainian negotiations.

a3415.speaker: KIIS, the leading Ukrainian polling institute (official figures)
a3415.name: KIIS
a3415.title: the leading Ukrainian polling institute (official figures)
a3415.speech: Official figures showing that the Ukrainian population now leans slightly in favour (55%) of ceding part of the territory if the concession can end the conflict.

a3680.speaker: Dr Christ Arsène Ouinsou, economist
a3680.name: Dr Christ Arsène Ouinsou
a3680.title: economist
a3680.speech: On how the AU obtained its G20 seat: said it all started on 20 September 2022, when Macky Sall, President of Senegal and Chairperson in office of the African Union, participated in the 77th ordinary session of the UN General Assembly in New York and called for “overcoming the reluctance and deconstructing the narratives that persist in confining Africa to the margins of decision-making circles”; said the request was made in a context in which, nearly eighty years after the birth of the UN System and the Bretton Woods Institutions, African countries are weakly represented in the major global decision-making bodies, even though decisions taken there also affect Africa; recalled that Sall had also called for the lifting of foreign sanctions against Zimbabwe.

a3680.speaker: Dr Christ Arsène Ouinsou, economist
a3680.name: Dr Christ Arsène Ouinsou
a3680.title: economist
a3680.speech: On the symbolism and effects of AU accession to the G20: said the accession is a sign of progress for the African continent in terms of its involvement in global governance, since the G20 is the leading forum for international economic cooperation and plays an important role in the formulation and global governance of major international economic issues, and “Africa can also make itself heard on the major socio-economic issues at the global level”; said the integration can allow African countries to intensify their economic and diplomatic ties with G20 member countries and increase trade with them, but warned that in the current context of the war between Ukraine and Russia, Africa also risks suffering along with the older G20 members if Russia takes a decision against the group.

a3680.speaker: Dr Christ Arsène Ouinsou, economist
a3680.name: Dr Christ Arsène Ouinsou
a3680.title: economist
a3680.speech: On the AU Commission's status: said the request could allow the AU Commission to enjoy the same rights as the other commissions of the group, increasing its involvement in the group's decision-making, and that if it is not governed by the same status, that could limit its participation in certain respects; on other bodies, said the AU has just joined one of the largest groupings in terms of global economic cooperation and that this would be sufficient for its participation in global governance.

a3680.speaker: Macky Sall, President of Senegal and Chairperson in office of the African Union
a3680.name: Macky Sall
a3680.title: President of Senegal and Chairperson in office of the African Union
a3680.speech: At the 77th ordinary session of the UN General Assembly on 20 September 2022, called for “overcoming the reluctance and deconstructing the narratives that persist in confining Africa to the margins of decision-making circles”; also called for the lifting of foreign sanctions against Zimbabwe.

a3688.speaker: South African Presidency (statement)
a3688.name: South African Presidency (statement)
a3688.speech: Says it has noted with regret the expulsion of its ambassador to Washington Mr. Ebrahim Rasool but urged calm in a statement ; responded to the expulsion on Saturday, calling it “regrettable” and urging all parties to maintain diplomatic decorum ; the administration in Pretoria will urge all relevant and impacted stakeholders to maintain the established diplomatic decorum in their engagement with the matter.

a3688.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a3688.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a3688.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a3688.speech: During a seminar vilified the Trump administration’s Make America Great Again (MAGA) doctrine, describing it as supremacist. He told seminarians that: “The supremacist assault on incumbency, we see it in the domestic politics of the USA, the MAGA movement — the Make America Great Again movement — as a response not simply to a supremacist instinct, but to very clear data that shows great demographic shifts in the USA in which the voting electorate in the USA is projected to become 48% white, and that the possibility of a majority of minorities is looming on the horizon”.

a3688.speaker: President Cyril Ramaphosa and the South African government
a3688.name: President Cyril Ramaphosa and the South African government
a3688.speech: Say they will remain committed to building a mutually beneficial relationship with the United States despite the expulsion of Mr Rasool.

a3688.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a3688.name: Marco Rubio
a3688.title: US Secretary of State
a3688.speech: Announced on Friday night that Rasool had been declared persona non grata, accusing him of being a “race-baiting politician” who harbours hostility toward America and President Donald Trump. “South Africa’s Ambassador to the United States is no longer welcome in our great country,” Rubio stated on social media platform X. “We have nothing to discuss with him and so he is considered PERSONA NON GRATA.”

a3688.speaker: Trump administration
a3688.name: Trump administration
a3688.speech: Cited South Africa’s land reform policies, which it claims unfairly target white farmers, as the reason for the aid suspension.

a3688.speaker: South Africa (government)
a3688.name: South Africa (government)
a3688.speech: Has denied these allegations, asserting that the reforms aim to address historical inequalities.

a3966.speaker: Umar Namadi, Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.name: Umar Namadi
a3966.title: Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.speech: Reaffirmed his administration's commitment to transforming the healthcare sector of Jigawa State; described the foundation laying as a historic and significant milestone in his administration's transformative journey for Greater Jigawa, stating that the strategic investments were part of the state's overarching vision to ensure long-term prosperity and enhance the socio-economic well-being of the people; emphasized that his administration's focus on health and education is central to the broader human development agenda ; "From our investing in expanding access through Community Health Insurance, under which over 143,000 vulnerable people were effectively covered, to revitalization and expansion of access to both primary and secondary healthcare services, to the development of human resources for the health sector, we are steadily fulfilling our pledge to the people of Jigawa State."

a3966.speaker: Umar Namadi, Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.name: Umar Namadi
a3966.title: Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.speech: Clarified that the newly built medical facilities aim to transform the state's approach to healthcare delivery: "Even though all the initial investments for these three projects would be through direct treasury funding, ultimately the plan is for these to be run based on a model of public-private-partnership arrangement with certified health investment firms"; said this model will ensure both managerial efficiency and long-term viability of the projects, adding that with the commissioning of these centres, the era of going to other states to obtain services such as mammography, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans, and many other specialized diagnostic health services will be over ; said his administration has a vision to position Dutse as a regional hub for health tourism, stating that the new facilities will serve not only Jigawa residents but also people from neighbouring states.

a3966.speaker: Umar Namadi, Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.name: Umar Namadi
a3966.title: Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.speech: Explained the unique features of the Cryo-Oxygen Plant, saying it will "not only provide 100% pure liquid medical oxygen for patients' needs but is also designed to produce nitrogen at commercial quantity, thereby creating another value chain for fertilizer companies in Nigeria"; added that the oxygen will be transported in branded, digitally optimised cylinders using electric vehicles to minimise cost and promote green energy.

a3966.speaker: Umar Namadi, Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.name: Umar Namadi
a3966.title: Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.speech: Mentioned the ongoing completion of the Orthopaedic Hospital in Gumel, specialist hospitals in Hadejia and Kazaure, and free dialysis services across several general hospitals, and disclosed that the government has approved free care services for diabetic, hypertensive, and sickle cell disease patients.

a3966.speaker: Umar Namadi, Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.name: Umar Namadi
a3966.title: Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.speech: On workforce development, stated: "This administration has recruited over 920 primary health care workers as well as another 200 secondary health care clinical staff, with an additional 1,000 PHC workers engaged on an ad-hoc basis"; urged health workers across the state to rededicate themselves to duty and ensure quality service delivery, noting that reports of laxity in healthcare facilities will no longer be tolerated.

a3966.speaker: Umar Namadi, Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.name: Umar Namadi
a3966.title: Governor of Jigawa State, Nigeria
a3966.speech: Expressed appreciation to development partners such as UNICEF, WHO, FCDO, USAID, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation for their contributions, as well as the traditional and religious leaders who continue to support health advocacy across the state.

a4031.speaker: Bryony Everett, Director of Global Programmes at DT Global UK
a4031.name: Bryony Everett
a4031.title: Director of Global Programmes at DT Global UK
a4031.speech: Emphasised the potential impact of the initiative at the launch.

a4107.speaker: Morris Wamah, Jr., LIDS Executive Director
a4107.name: Morris Wamah
a4107.title: Jr., LIDS Executive Director
a4107.speech: said the project seeks to enhance citizens' capacities on the Local Government Act, sharpening their participation skills in domestic revenue mobilization, and service delivery at the community level in Bong county. He averred that the project expects a significant increase in budget transparency through the inclusion of local leaders into budgetary processes and decision-making to ensure the quality delivery of basic social services in rural Liberia ; “This Project has three major objectives, and they include an improvement in Domestic resources mobilization, an increase in budget transparency, and an improved local development and Service delivery at the Community levels” ; He expressed optimism that when the project is completed, residents of beneficiary communities will have a broad-base knowledge on government functionaries especially at the Community levels ; said this first phase of the project targets several communities in five administrative districts in Bong County, including Kpaai, Jorquelleh 1&2, Zota, and Sanoyea, respectively.

a4107.speaker: Albert J. Thompson, Citizens Participation Officer at LEAD
a4107.name: Albert J. Thompson
a4107.title: Citizens Participation Officer at LEAD
a4107.speech: encouraged residents of the project communities to take advantage of the project if they should be included in the national decision-making processes of our country. He expressed hope that when the project is completed, residents of the beneficiary communities will have a broad-based knowledge of government functionaries, especially at the community level.

a4107.speaker: Stakeholders at the launch (Commissioners, Paramount and Clan Chiefs, youth and women leaders, local NGOs, and Bong County Superintendent Hawa L. Norris)
a4107.name: Stakeholders at the launch (Commissioners
a4107.title: Paramount and Clan Chiefs, youth and women leaders, local NGOs, and Bong County Superintendent Hawa L. Norris)
a4107.speech: They extended commendations to LEAD and its implementing partners for the initiative, describing it as “an eye-opener”. They pledged their commitment of taking crucial advantage in order to improve their respective Communities. They further promised to take ownership of the project.

a4150.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4150.name: Abiy Ahmed
a4150.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4150.speech: Said that landlocked Ethiopia has no intention of starting a war with neighbouring Eritrea in order to gain access to the sea, and that the issue of sea access should be resolved through diplomacy and mutual benefit: “Our intention is to negotiate based on the principle of give and take. What the Eritrean people need is development, not conflict. Our plan is not to fight but to work together and grow together.” ; Stressed that discussions around a seaport should not be taboo and that global norms support the idea that large nations require maritime access ; In a previous statement in 2023, said that having a seaport was an “existential issue” for the nation.

a4150.speaker: Getachew Reda, Tigray's Interim President
a4150.name: Getachew Reda
a4150.title: Tigray's Interim President
a4150.speech: Accused his rivals of colluding with Eritrea: “We have reason to believe external actors are involved,” alleging that Eritrea sees turmoil in Tigray as an opportunity for its own interests.

a4150.speaker: Osman Saleh, Eritrea's Foreign Minister
a4150.name: Osman Saleh
a4150.title: Eritrea's Foreign Minister
a4150.speech: Dismissed these allegations, telling diplomats in the capital, Asmara, on Tuesday that his country “categorically rejects” any claims that it is involved in northern Ethiopia’s tensions.

a4150.speaker: Gedion Timotewos, Ethiopia's Foreign Minister
a4150.name: Gedion Timotewos
a4150.title: Ethiopia's Foreign Minister
a4150.speech: Told diplomats in Addis Ababa that his government suspects one of the factions in Tigray has links to Eritrea, though he did not provide specific details.

a4175.speaker: US Treasury Department (statement)
a4175.name: US Treasury Department (statement)
a4175.speech: Announced on Tuesday in a statement: “The United States has followed through on its October commitment (...), by transferring these funds” into the World Bank's intermediary fund dedicated to Ukraine, “through which they will be made available to Ukraine.”

a4175.speaker: Janet Yellen, US Treasury Secretary
a4175.name: Janet Yellen
a4175.title: US Treasury Secretary
a4175.speech: “These funds - financed by the extraordinary revenues from Russia's immobilised assets - will provide Ukraine with essential support.”

a4175.speaker: Donald Trump, US president-elect
a4175.name: Donald Trump
a4175.title: US president-elect
a4175.speech: Has hammered home his intention to reduce American aid to Ukraine; repeated that Kyiv should expect “probably” less aid from the United States, in an interview broadcast on Sunday.

a4270.speaker: United Nations Refugee Agency (UNHCR)
a4270.name: United Nations Refugee Agency (UNHCR)
a4270.speech: Said on Friday that the escalation of violence in eastern DRC has already caused the displacement of more than 230,000 people since the beginning of the year, and said it was alarmed by the worsening violence in North and South Kivu provinces ; in a statement explained that the escalation of clashes between non-state armed groups and the Congolese army in these two provinces is intensifying one of the world's most alarming and under-reported humanitarian crises, marked by widespread human rights violations and massive forced displacement.

a4270.speaker: UNHCR
a4270.name: UNHCR
a4270.speech: Said it was ready to assist these populations as soon as access is restored, and stressed the urgency of responding to the escalating humanitarian crisis.

a4270.speaker: Local government of Fizi territory, South Kivu
a4270.name: Local government of Fizi territory
a4270.title: South Kivu
a4270.speech: Reports that 84,000 people are now displaced and has requested humanitarian aid from the international community.

a4270.speaker: Eujin Byun, UNHCR spokesperson
a4270.name: Eujin Byun
a4270.title: UNHCR spokesperson
a4270.speech: "Fighters are using people's homes as shelters, putting residents at risk, blurring the distinction between combatants and civilians," she said at a press briefing in Geneva.

a4270.speaker: Eujin Byun, UNHCR spokesperson
a4270.name: Eujin Byun
a4270.title: UNHCR spokesperson
a4270.speech: "Safe and unhindered access for humanitarian workers must be guaranteed, and measures to protect civilians - especially women and children - must be prioritised" ; recalled that UNHCR needs a total of $226 million this year to address the protracted emergency in the DRC, and that to date it has received less than 10% of the funds required.

a4270.speaker: United Nations Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO) in the DRC
a4270.name: United Nations Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO) in the DRC
a4270.speech: Warned that two years after the start of the intercommunal conflict in Tshopo province cohabitation remains difficult between the communities in conflict, noting that this could constitute a major risk to the province's stability.

a4270.speaker: UNJHRO report (fact-finding mission, August 2024)
a4270.name: UNJHRO report (fact-finding mission
a4270.title: August 2024)
a4270.speech: Recorded 228 victims of human rights abuses committed by armed civilian attackers from the Mbole or Lengola communities and their allies, of whom 149 were killed and 39 injured or subjected to inhuman and degrading treatment causing permanent disabilities ; "The suspects in the abuses were unanimously identified as young men speaking in the majority of cases Mbole/Lingala or Swahili/Lengola. They carried firearms, machetes, knives and poisoned arrows," the report details, stressing that the Mbole groups in particular have reached a certain level of internal organisation and chain of command.

a4270.speaker: Government and humanitarian sources
a4270.name: Government and humanitarian sources
a4270.speech: According to them, at least 107,000 people have been displaced because of the conflict and live in very precarious conditions in three displacement sites in Kisangani and in the commune of Lubunga.

a4435.speaker: Colin Deiner, head of the Western Cape's disaster management service
a4435.name: Colin Deiner
a4435.title: head of the Western Cape's disaster management service
a4435.speech: According to Deiner, in De Doorns more than 50 informal homes were washed away during flooding, houses and businesses in the area were also damaged, and a wastewater treatment works was flooded ; "Mopping-up operations are under way," Deiner said ; Said assessments were under way to establish the extent of the damage, but added that the West Coast, Cape Winelands and Breederiver Valley were affected the most.

a4435.speaker: Colin Deiner, head of the Western Cape's disaster management service
a4435.name: Colin Deiner
a4435.title: head of the Western Cape's disaster management service
a4435.speech: Said a South African Weather Service (SAWS) warning would be in place until 22:00 on Tuesday.

a4435.speaker: South African Weather Service (SAWS)
a4435.name: South African Weather Service (SAWS)
a4435.speech: Has warned that severe thunderstorms and possible heavy downpours are forecast for parts of Gauteng, the Free State, Mpumalanga, the Eastern Cape and the Western Cape on Tuesday.

a4538.speaker: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) projections (July 2025)
a4538.name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) projections (July 2025)
a4538.speech: According to new OECD projections, official development assistance could fall by as much as 17% this year, continuing a trend already begun in 2024; the OECD anticipates a further drop in net aid in 2025 of between 9% and 17%, representing in absolute terms a loss of 56 billion dollars in only two years; bilateral aid to sub-Saharan Africa could fall by 16% to 28% in 2025, a return to levels comparable to the mid-2000s; humanitarian aid financing could decline by up to 36% between 2023 and 2025 and education aid by 18% to 22%.

a4538.speaker: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
a4538.name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
a4538.speech: Estimates that, after a fall of 40% in 2023 and of 6% in 2024, health financing in sub-Saharan Africa could fall by a further 14% to 29% in 2025.

a4819.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (statement)
a4819.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (statement)
