a4819.speech: Said in its statement that the humanitarian situation, in which living conditions are severely degraded, is the result of hunger caused by the armed conflict that has lasted about 16 months and aggravated by flooding ; stressed that international experts of the Famine Review Committee formally confirmed on Thursday “the existence of famine conditions in the Zamzam camp, near the town of Al Fasher, in North Darfur, where half a million displaced people live” ; said the camp is experiencing an extreme food shortage, which has caused an exponential rise in malnutrition and mortality rates ; “Almost all internally displaced people in Sudan (97%) are in localities with acute levels of food insecurity or worse.”

a4819.speaker: Famine Review Committee (international experts)
a4819.name: Famine Review Committee (international experts)
a4819.speech: Formally confirmed on Thursday the existence of famine conditions in the Zamzam camp, near the town of Al Fasher, in North Darfur, where half a million displaced people live.

a4819.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (statement)
a4819.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (statement)
a4819.speech: Said the latest figures show that displacement continues to increase, with more than 10.7 million people seeking safety in the country, many of them displaced two or more times ; “In the past month alone, the fighting in Sennar state displaced more than 700,000 people, 63% of whom were originally displaced from other states, most of them from Khartoum, the capital” ; said the situation is being aggravated by the widespread flooding which, since June, has displaced more than 20,000 people in 11 of Sudan’s 18 states ; “Essential infrastructure has been washed away, further disrupting the delivery of vital humanitarian assistance.”

a4819.speaker: Othman Belbeisi, IOM Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa
a4819.name: Othman Belbeisi
a4819.title: IOM Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa
a4819.speech: “Let us not be mistaken, these conditions will persist and worsen if the conflict and the restrictions on humanitarian access continue” ; pointed out that without an immediate global response there is a risk of tens of thousands of avoidable deaths in the coming months ; “We are at a breaking point, a catastrophic and cataclysmic breaking point.”

a4819.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (statement)
a4819.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM) (statement)
a4819.speech: Said humanitarian and protection conditions in Sudan are among the worst in the world: “The ongoing conflict is marked by appalling levels of human rights violations, ethnic persecution, massacres of civilian populations and gender-based violence” ; warned that over the next three months an estimated 25.6 million people will face acute food insecurity as the conflict spreads and coping mechanisms are exhausted ; explained that restrictions on humanitarian access, including impediments imposed by the parties to the conflict, have seriously limited aid organisations’ ability to save lives, especially during the current rainy season ; urged: “Urgent funding is needed to scale up the response and reach those who still desperately need food, shelter, water, health services and specialised protection.”

a4905.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect
a4905.name: Donald Trump
a4905.title: US President-elect
a4905.speech: Announced on Monday that Republican congresswoman Elise Stefanik would be the next US ambassador to the United Nations, and also announced that he would appoint Tom Homan as the top official in charge of the borders, whom he calls the “border czar” ; Trump considers Stefanik “tough and smart for America”.

a4905.speaker: Elise Stefanik, Republican congresswoman, US ambassador-designate to the UN
a4905.name: Elise Stefanik
a4905.title: Republican congresswoman, US ambassador-designate to the UN
a4905.speech: “In my conversation with President Trump, I expressed how deeply honoured I was to accept his nomination and my willingness to secure the support of my colleagues in the United States Senate,” she said, quoted by CNN Brasil.

a4905.speaker: CNN (cited)
a4905.name: CNN (cited)
a4905.speech: Cited as saying that Stefanik “has been a strong ally of the president-elect and an important fundraiser for the Republican Party”.

a5229.speaker: David Kihenzile, Deputy Minister for Transport of Tanzania
a5229.name: David Kihenzile
a5229.title: Deputy Minister for Transport of Tanzania
a5229.speech: acknowledged the challenges posed by rising water levels after visiting Kasanga Port on Tuesday, calling for urgent action to protect the country’s strategic ports along Lake Tanganyika: “The government is planning a short-term solution to restore operations at the terminal, while the long-term solution involves raising the berth up by adding additional layers” ; further said the 5.5 metres berth at Kabwe port is also submerged in water.

a5229.speaker: Eng Abdallah Mohammed, Acting Lake Tanganyika Ports Manager
a5229.name: Eng Abdallah Mohammed
a5229.title: Acting Lake Tanganyika Ports Manager
a5229.speech: told the Deputy Minister that the water levels are coming in fast threatening the two storage facilities and that some of 450 tonnes of cement have been damaged by water at Kasanga port ; “The refurbishment of the port coincided with the construction of a major road connecting Kasanga and Sumbawanga town, which has increased traffic to the port.”

a5229.speaker: Humphrey Kachimile, Acting Kasanga Port Officer
a5229.name: Humphrey Kachimile
a5229.title: Acting Kasanga Port Officer
a5229.speech: said that the port primarily handles 3,500 tonnes of cement monthly from Mbeya Cement for export to the DRC and Zambia: ‘Mbeya Cement is our biggest customer, regularly exporting cement to the DRC via this port.’

a5404.speaker: Indermit Gill, World Bank chief economist and senior vice president for development economics, and M. Ayhan Kose, World Bank deputy chief economist and director of the Prospects Group (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a5404.name: Indermit Gill
a5404.title: World Bank chief economist and senior vice president for development economics, and M. Ayhan Kose, World Bank deputy chief economist and director of the Prospects Group (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a5404.speech: Ask whether the world can afford to turn a blind eye to the plight of the 28 poorest nations, arguing that "the poorest countries are in desperate straits, and the rest of the world is looking the other way"; note that at the end of June the combined GDP of the 28 low-income countries was roughly half a trillion dollars in a 100 trillion dollar global economy, that 700 million people live in these countries with about half in extreme poverty, that their governments spend about 50pc more on war and defence than healthcare and devote a mere three percent of total government spending to supporting the most vulnerable citizens, and that key human development indicators - maternal mortality 25pc higher, electricity access down from 52pc to barely 40pc, average life expectancy of 62 years - are far worse now than in the low-income countries of 2000.

a5404.speaker: Indermit Gill, World Bank chief economist and senior vice president for development economics, and M. Ayhan Kose, World Bank deputy chief economist and director of the Prospects Group (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a5404.name: Indermit Gill
a5404.title: World Bank chief economist and senior vice president for development economics, and M. Ayhan Kose, World Bank deputy chief economist and director of the Prospects Group (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a5404.speech: Argue that "wealthier countries have chosen the wrong moment to become less generous": even before the pandemic, foreign aid flows to the poorest countries, especially in Sub-Saharan Africa, were slowing, and today wealthier countries are redirecting more of their foreign aid budgets to meet the surge of refugees arriving on their shores; note that grants fell from about one-third of government revenues in 2011-2015 to less than one-fifth, that government debt-to-GDP ratios soared from 36pc in 2011 to 67pc last year, and that fourteen low-income countries are now in debt distress or at high risk.

a5404.speaker: Indermit Gill, World Bank chief economist and senior vice president for development economics, and M. Ayhan Kose, World Bank deputy chief economist and director of the Prospects Group (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a5404.name: Indermit Gill
a5404.title: World Bank chief economist and senior vice president for development economics, and M. Ayhan Kose, World Bank deputy chief economist and director of the Prospects Group (commentary provided by Project Syndicate)
a5404.speech: Urge that as global leaders gather in New York for the United Nations Summit on Sustainable Development Goals they must not forget the fundamental promise of the SDGs, "to reach the furthest behind first," and that wealthier countries and all international financial institutions should move decisively on three fronts: increasing concessional financing and enlarging the pool of resources available to multilateral development banks; accelerating debt restructuring, since the Common Framework's "glacial pace" has deterred countries from seeking relief; and doubling down on the reform agenda by helping low-income countries mobilise domestic revenues, improve spending efficiency and debt management, build human capital and ease impediments to private investment; warn that "time is running out" and that the suffering of millions "is contagious and already spilling over national borders, with unpredictable global consequences."

a5597.speaker: HRM Ugoeze Chigbo Nwamara, founder of Off The Hook Foundation For Rural Dwellers
a5597.name: HRM Ugoeze Chigbo Nwamara
a5597.title: founder of Off The Hook Foundation For Rural Dwellers
a5597.speech: According to the founder, the Foundation, established a decade ago, had so far equipped more than 5,000 widows with practical skills, thus leading many to establish thriving businesses and achieve financial independence ; "A standpoint achievement was in 2018 when the 'Off The Hook Foundation' in partnership with USAID trained and empowered 108 young widows out of 2,000 in attendance who received sewing machines, baking equipment and much more, allowing them to launch successful businesses, many of which are flourishing today."

a5597.speaker: HRM Ugoeze Chigbo Nwamara, founder of Off The Hook Foundation For Rural Dwellers
a5597.name: HRM Ugoeze Chigbo Nwamara
a5597.title: founder of Off The Hook Foundation For Rural Dwellers
a5597.speech: "We have provided assistance to our youths by helping them with school feeds and registration for WASC examinations ensuring they have access to education and opportunity for a brighter future and we have constructed safe housing for vulnerable widows and the elderly." ; added that the medical outreach of the organisation, in collaboration with its partner Medical and Humanitarian Aide for Africa (MAHAFA), had provided free healthcare services to over 5,000 widows and their duties.

a5597.speaker: HRM Ugoeze Chigbo Nwamara, founder of Off The Hook Foundation For Rural Dwellers
a5597.name: HRM Ugoeze Chigbo Nwamara
a5597.title: founder of Off The Hook Foundation For Rural Dwellers
a5597.speech: While assuring that her NGO is committed to expanding its services, innovative programmes, advocacy and awareness in future, said: "Let us unite in our efforts to create a world where no woman suffers in silence; no elder is left behind and every youth is given the opportunity to thrive."

a5891.speaker: Joël Akowanou, Director of Operations of MCA-Benin II
a5891.name: Joël Akowanou
a5891.title: Director of Operations of MCA-Benin II
a5891.speech: “We are therefore in a transition towards an intelligent system where we can intervene very quickly on the network and control consumption, production…”

a5891.speaker: Gérard Zagrodnik, Director General of the Beninese Electric Energy Company (Sbee); Brian Shukan, US Ambassador to Benin; Alice Albright, CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC); and Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, Minister of State
a5891.name: Gérard Zagrodnik
a5891.title: Director General of the Beninese Electric Energy Company (Sbee); Brian Shukan, US Ambassador to Benin; Alice Albright, CEO of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC); and Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, Minister of State
a5891.speech: Each in turn welcomed the fact that this infrastructure is a first for Benin.

a5891.speaker: Gérard Zagrodnik, Director General of Sbee
a5891.name: Gérard Zagrodnik
a5891.title: Director General of Sbee
a5891.speech: Presented to the audience the centre’s mission and its energy and economic advantages for Benin: “The mission of the centre is to ensure the balance between production and consumption at the lowest cost, under optimal conditions of safety and quality (…). This centre has extremely important responsibilities, notably the steering, monitoring and remote control of installations, and the management of supply and demand (…). It therefore plays a leading role in the use of the investments that have been made in recent years. With its capacity for modelling and simulating the network, this centre will also make it possible to optimise future investments, to run simulations before investing, to evaluate, to find options…”

a5891.speaker: Brian Shukan, US Ambassador to Benin
a5891.name: Brian Shukan
a5891.title: US Ambassador to Benin
a5891.speech: Added that the site “we could also call it the command and control centre of Benin’s electricity network. In this operations centre, which works 24 hours a day, 7 days a week (…), operators are trained to identify and resolve faults in the Beninese electricity network…”

a5891.speaker: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, Minister of State in charge of Development and Coordination of Government Action and chairman of the board of MCA-Benin II
a5891.name: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané
a5891.title: Minister of State in charge of Development and Coordination of Government Action and chairman of the board of MCA-Benin II
a5891.speech: Set out some of the advantages of the facility: “It is a centre that will allow us to better master the distribution of energy in our country and to substantially reduce the duration of outages/load shedding…”

a5891.speaker: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané, Minister of State (on behalf of the government)
a5891.name: Abdoulaye Bio Tchané
a5891.title: Minister of State (on behalf of the government)
a5891.speech: Renewed Benin’s commitment to sustaining all of the compact’s gains so that everyone, without distinction, has access to reliable, good-quality and lower-cost electricity for the country’s socio-economic development.

a6020.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Minister of Industrialisation and Trade of Namibia
a6020.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a6020.title: Minister of Industrialisation and Trade of Namibia
a6020.speech: Said a number of export markets have been secured for Namibian exporters, including in Africa, and encouraged all local producers to seize opportunities of continental access: "Hence, the call is now upon you, entrepreneurs, to work hard and utilise the opportunity made available for you to thrive globally and contribute to the country's foreign exchange reserves through export earnings."

a6020.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Minister of Industrialisation and Trade of Namibia
a6020.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a6020.title: Minister of Industrialisation and Trade of Namibia
a6020.speech: Said Namibia has an open economy that is susceptible to global market competition and that the country has been experiencing a negative balance of payment over the years due to imports exceeding exports as a result of a limited production basket: "Besides high-tech products and consumables, which forms part of Namibia's main imports, Namibia continues to import large quantities of basic commodities and other products that our business community can venture into. There is, therefore, an opportunity for Namibia to increase production capacity - and, as a result, increase exports."

a6020.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Minister of Industrialisation and Trade of Namibia
a6020.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a6020.title: Minister of Industrialisation and Trade of Namibia
a6020.speech: Said one of the notable trade arrangements Namibia currently focusses on is the market opportunity for products into the US under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) ; Said Namibia continues to appreciate continuous support from the USAID TradeHub, which has assisted Namibia in developing an AGOA utilisation strategy that seeks to increase Namibia's exports under the AGOA programme, allowing Namibia to export over 6 400 products duty-free to the United States.

a6020.speaker: Lucia Iipumbu, Minister of Industrialisation and Trade of Namibia
a6020.name: Lucia Iipumbu
a6020.title: Minister of Industrialisation and Trade of Namibia
a6020.speech: "Despite several economic challenges that face our people, this event seeks to recognise the outstanding performance and extraordinary efforts by our business people who make strides in overcoming market entry hurdles and achieving successful and consistent trade."

a6086.speaker: Chuku Mogotsi, self-described community leader in Tembisa
a6086.name: Chuku Mogotsi
a6086.title: self-described community leader in Tembisa
a6086.speech: says the violent protests that rocked the township are far from over ; says they will keep protesting until their grievances are attended to ; Addressing the media in Hospital View, said residents would continue protesting until the Ekurhuleni Municipality attended to their grievances.

a6086.speaker: Chuku Mogotsi, self-described community leader in Tembisa
a6086.name: Chuku Mogotsi
a6086.title: self-described community leader in Tembisa
a6086.speech: added many could not afford to pay their rates and taxes. "We are spending a lot of money on electricity. Our tariffs are skyrocketing. Our municipal rates are too high and we can't afford them. The municipality has cancelled the free units they used to give us." ; "We are pulling hard. We then decided to write a letter of demand to the mayor. We need lower rates. We need a flat rate. The municipality has to reinstate the indigent policy."

a6086.speaker: Chuku Mogotsi, self-described community leader in Tembisa
a6086.name: Chuku Mogotsi
a6086.title: self-described community leader in Tembisa
a6086.speech: blames Mayor Tania Campbell for the protests ; She said the protests escalated after residents felt Mayor Tania Campbell failed to address them when asked.

a6086.speaker: Chuku Mogotsi, self-described community leader in Tembisa
a6086.name: Chuku Mogotsi
a6086.title: self-described community leader in Tembisa
a6086.speech: "We are peaceful. We won't harm anyone. We are not violent. We managed to convince the police that we are not violent. I don't condone what happened in parts of the township."

a6086.speaker: Letlhogonolo Moseki, Community Safety MMC
a6086.name: Letlhogonolo Moseki
a6086.title: Community Safety MMC
a6086.speech: said the province had deployed more than 100 Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Police Department officers to Tembisa ; added they would be monitoring the situation.

a6086.speaker: Lebogang Maile, Gauteng Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs MEC
a6086.name: Lebogang Maile
a6086.title: Gauteng Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs MEC
a6086.speech: claimed he wanted to establish the cause of the violent protests.

a6212.speaker: Kogi State Police Command
a6212.name: Kogi State Police Command
a6212.speech: Confirmed the recovery of the body of photojournalist Ayobami Aiyepeku, allegedly killed by his neighbour, Oluwapelumi Adebayo.

a6212.speaker: SP Williams Aya, Kogi State Police Command spokesperson
a6212.name: SP Williams Aya
a6212.title: Kogi State Police Command spokesperson
a6212.speech: Told journalists on Monday in Lokoja that Aiyepeku’s decomposing body was discovered Sunday evening near the WAEC office in the Crusher Zone 8 axis of Lokoja: “The corpse has been deposited at the Kogi State Specialist Hospital,” adding that a discreet investigation is underway to uncover the full circumstances of the killing ; Appealed to the public, the deceased’s colleagues, and family to provide credible information that could aid the investigation.

a6212.speaker: Timothy Aiyepeku, elder brother of the deceased journalist
a6212.name: Timothy Aiyepeku
a6212.title: elder brother of the deceased journalist
a6212.speech: Urged the federal and Kogi governments to ensure justice is served: “We commend the police for their efforts so far and the media for ensuring this case remains in the public eye.”

a6212.speaker: Abdullahi Adamu, Chairman of Lokoja Local Government
a6212.name: Abdullahi Adamu
a6212.title: Chairman of Lokoja Local Government
a6212.speech: Visited the scene with security agents and confirmed the identity of the deceased.

a6242.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Minister of Finance of Tanzania
a6242.name: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba
a6242.title: Minister of Finance of Tanzania
a6242.speech: Said in his presentation to Parliament of the Proposals for the Government Budget Framework and Ceiling for 2025/2026 that the Government has proposed to collect and spend a total of Sh57.04 trillion in 2025/26, an increase of 13.4 percent compared with the 2024/25 budget of Sh50.29 trillion.

a6242.speaker: Dr Abel Kinyondo, lecturer in Economics at the University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM)
a6242.name: Dr Abel Kinyondo
a6242.title: lecturer in Economics at the University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM)
a6242.speech: Said that this year Tanzanians should expect a budget directed more towards election matters and completing implementation of the CCM manifesto: “So the election will take a large share, not just working tools but also the things around it – security, stability – and apart from that there are still strategic projects ongoing, including the Standard Gauge Railway (SGR)” ; said it is a budget to finish off the election manifesto promises so the Government can say it promised and delivered ; “Basically the big things, and those we see in this year's election manifesto promising things such as a new Constitution and so on, are things that will come in the coming financial year.”

a6242.speaker: Dr Lutengano Mwinuka, lecturer and economist at the University of Dodoma (UDOM)
a6242.name: Dr Lutengano Mwinuka
a6242.title: lecturer and economist at the University of Dodoma (UDOM)
a6242.speech: Said that in planning Tanzania tries to do well but there is still a need to look at implementation: “The implementation stage needs to be looked at carefully so that what is planned is implemented, and to look at the available sources of funds; you may plan but lack the sources of funds to implement” ; said there is also a need to look at cheap sources of funds that are not a burden to the nation, meaning concessional loans and reducing high-interest commercial loans.

a6242.speaker: Dr Lutengano Mwinuka, lecturer and economist at the University of Dodoma (UDOM)
a6242.name: Dr Lutengano Mwinuka
a6242.title: lecturer and economist at the University of Dodoma (UDOM)
a6242.speech: On the health sector, said the expectation is to see how the Government has prepared to implement the Universal Health Insurance Act, which aims to enable all citizens to access health services: “The revenue sources mentioned are excise duty on carbonated drinks, spirits, cosmetics, gaming taxes, motor vehicle insurance fees and revenue from electronic transaction levies.”

a6242.speaker: Dr Samwel Ogillo, Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Private Health Facilities in Tanzania (APHFTA)
a6242.name: Dr Samwel Ogillo
a6242.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Association of Private Health Facilities in Tanzania (APHFTA)
a6242.speech: Said their expectation is to see the Main Budget bring relief to the private sector so it can invest more in the health sector to serve those whose numbers will grow after getting insurance; said the health budget has a good direction because the universal health plan has shown a clearly visible direction, although there is concern because the country's economy is low and national resources are not enough to run it fully: “We believe that at least when the Main Budget comes it will have a vision of ensuring that at least some funds are directed straight to implementing the universal health plan – but the cry of poor citizens: how will they benefit?” ; “Once many have health insurance they will seek treatment; those who go to traditional healers will go to hospitals, and when people increase the hospitals will not be enough.”

a6242.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a6242.name: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko
a6242.title: President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a6242.speech: Said the ministry's budget has been passed at Sh1.61 trillion, so the expectation is that it will support the provision of services and their sustainability, especially those provided under the funding of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID): “We expect this budget will be able to build resilience so that we have the ability to procure our own things and to order those ARV, tuberculosis and malaria medicines. It will help efforts to implement services that support universal health insurance; our expectation is to hear the Main Budget state this as well, along with employing workers. We expect our 10 priorities to be implemented with this budget.”

a6242.speaker: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko, President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a6242.name: Dr Mugisha Nkoronko
a6242.title: President of the Medical Association of Tanzania (MAT)
a6242.speech: Said the worry of many is that every year the Government does not fulfil the budget at service delivery facilities; said implementation in past years has been between 60 and 70 percent and the budget has never reached 100 percent; advised that systems be put right and then used, as the doctors' association and others promoting health services have done.

a6242.speaker: Mwajuma Ramadhani, resident of Kisosora in Tanga city
a6242.name: Mwajuma Ramadhani
a6242.title: resident of Kisosora in Tanga city
a6242.speech: Expects priority on education, especially free education, and sees the importance of investment in repairing school furniture to match the number of students: “If possible, the budget should look at how to set aside a fund that will help repair schools in cooperation with citizens, but also to add desks, because children are sitting on the floor after the increase in students due to the free education policy.”

a6242.speaker: Robert Kimaro, trader at Tangamano market in Tanga region
a6242.name: Robert Kimaro
a6242.title: trader at Tangamano market in Tanga region
a6242.speech: Said he would like to see the budget directed at improving the market environment: “Some of us traders have been registered and recognised by the Government regarding our businesses, but it has been a challenge to get loans; the budget should look, through the Ministry of Industry and Trade, at setting up a special window for us to borrow, like college students do, and afterwards we repay their money under an arrangement that will be set.”

a6242.speaker: James Kisemo, resident of Tabata in Dar es Salaam
a6242.name: James Kisemo
a6242.title: resident of Tabata in Dar es Salaam
a6242.speech: Said Tanzanians are eagerly awaiting the Main Budget, looking to see how the government will address various social and economic challenges: “We expect to see strong government strategies in dealing with the challenges of the health sector, especially after the departure of some donors such as USAID. The expectation is that the budget will direct more resources to improving health services and ensuring the availability of essential equipment and medicines.”

a6242.speaker: Petro Noel, resident of Nyegezi in Mwanza city
a6242.name: Petro Noel
a6242.title: resident of Nyegezi in Mwanza city
a6242.speech: Said he expects the Government to come with a plan to widen the tax base that will help increase revenue: “Currently, those who verifiably pay tax are employees in the formal sector... while a large number of Tanzanians who are self-employed in the informal sector are left outside the tax system. This causes the tax burden to fall on a few. Because of low education and awareness of tax matters, some small traders find themselves using part of their capital to pay tax even before doing business and making a profit. It is important that tax be paid from profit and not capital” ; advised the Government to put in place a system to control tax evasion loopholes among traders and investors with large capital ; “I also expect the Government will reduce or completely remove taxes and levies on low-income Tanzanians, including small traders and vendors in markets, auctions and periodic markets... This is not fair, because this group is forced to leave home with levy money regardless of whether they will sell their goods or not.”

a6242.speaker: Jasimin Kulwa, resident of Iseni in Mwanza city
a6242.name: Jasimin Kulwa
a6242.title: resident of Iseni in Mwanza city
a6242.speech: Said she expects the budget to focus on easing citizens' pain, especially making the price of essential needs match what a Tanzanian earns per month: “I don't expect to be given more burden; right now life has become very expensive, essential needs are high compared with the money we earn in our jobs... it has reached a point where when you receive your salary it all goes on paying debts. You would say we work for lending institutions or for the shopkeepers in our neighbourhoods.”

a6242.speaker: Revina Costantine, resident of Uyole in Mbeya city and entrepreneur
a6242.name: Revina Costantine
a6242.title: resident of Uyole in Mbeya city and entrepreneur
a6242.speech: Said a large budget should be directed to health, road infrastructure and water because those are the areas complained about: “The costs of treatment, especially for us of low income – we would like to hear that on the health side we get relief; but also many roads are bad and in many areas there is no water service.”

a6242.speaker: Conchesta Rwamlaza, Special Seats Member of Parliament
a6242.name: Conchesta Rwamlaza
a6242.title: Special Seats Member of Parliament
a6242.speech: Said she expects the budget to answer citizens' problems including road infrastructure, education, health and other social groups, especially the elderly: “Let's say the budget should bring together all groups, it should leave no one behind – that is what the good things in a budget should be. The budget has risen now, so I have expectations that it will be able to help answer” ; “But also to ensure there is no such thing as children dropping out – to ensure that whoever is supposed to finish standard seven or form four finishes” ; said the country cannot invest in education and then have children who do not finish their studies.

a6242.speaker: Dr Benson Bagonza, Bishop of the Karagwe Diocese of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Tanzania (ELCT)
a6242.name: Dr Benson Bagonza
a6242.title: Bishop of the Karagwe Diocese of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Tanzania (ELCT)
a6242.speech: Said he does not expect to see any change in the budget if the issue of corruption is not properly addressed: “I am not attracted by the new budget; even if they brought back the one that is ending I would not have much trouble. My big problem is that the level of corruption and misuse of funds has increased; whatever good budget you come with, if you have not dealt with corruption it cannot be productive. People are eating public money as if they have no good sense. There is no miracle other than dealing with corruption; I wish to see all leaders condemn corruption – right now corruption is condemning the leaders. The source of this is the absence of good governance; the administration should be accountable to the citizens, unlike now.”

a6242.speaker: Sheikh Khamis Mataka, Chairman of the Council of the National Muslim Council of Tanzania (BAKWATA)
a6242.name: Sheikh Khamis Mataka
a6242.title: Chairman of the Council of the National Muslim Council of Tanzania (BAKWATA)
a6242.speech: Said he expects a budget that will address important areas including completing the universal health insurance process to bring relief to Tanzanians who cannot afford treatment costs; wanted the price of kerosene looked at because the commodity is still relied on by poor families; and wanted the Government to conduct a census of traders and owners of taxable resources in order to widen the tax base.

a6242.speaker: Elieth Mtaita, pastor of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Tanzania (ELCT), Boay Parish, Manyara region
a6242.name: Elieth Mtaita
a6242.title: pastor of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Tanzania (ELCT), Boay Parish, Manyara region
a6242.speech: Said what should be addressed in the budget is cutting spending, especially on things that do not involve development: “Convoys of leaders' vehicles should be reduced and money should be increased for development projects such as road construction, water projects for citizens, and medicines and medical equipment should be taken to hospitals. We have seen MPs proposing that people be deducted money on phones; why don't we look at MPs' allowances, and even their salaries being reduced, in order to bring services to citizens, because those MPs serve the citizens” ; said the social services sectors should be given more budget than at present because that is the way to improve citizens' lives.

a6242.speaker: Samson Sombi, teacher in Morogoro region
a6242.name: Samson Sombi
a6242.title: teacher in Morogoro region
a6242.speech: Said that often in an election year a lot of money is directed to the election, but it is important that the education sector be looked at in depth: “We have new curricula that need implementation; funds must be set aside to employ teachers and give them seminars on how to implement these curricula; equipment matching the new curricula must be bought, along with improving learning environments” ; said that since the country depends on farmers and pastoralists it is important to grow their economy: “If those are achieved, farmers will farm productively and get rid of conflicts between farmers and pastoralists.”

a6274.speaker: James Gatwech Jock, Commissioner of Nasir County, Upper Nile State
a6274.name: James Gatwech Jock
a6274.title: Commissioner of Nasir County, Upper Nile State
a6274.speech: Has denied reports that government-distributed relief food is contaminated; described the claims circulating among community members as “false and baseless”; assured the public that the food items, which include beans, sorghum, and salt, have been tested and confirmed safe for human consumption: “We heard about those allegations from other people who said two things: first of all, they said that the food had been poisoned by the government of South Sudan; another thing, they said the food was given to the soldiers. These two allegations are not correct” ; said the government would not endanger the lives of its citizens by distributing unsafe food.

a6274.speaker: James Gatwech Jock, Commissioner of Nasir County, Upper Nile State
a6274.name: James Gatwech Jock
a6274.title: Commissioner of Nasir County, Upper Nile State
a6274.speech: Did not specify how many people have received the relief items so far, but confirmed that three airdrops have reached Nasir: “We received the food yesterday (Sunday, 25/05/2025), today (Monday, 26/05/2025), and the day before yesterday (Saturday, 24/05/2025). Now I think they landed three times” ; “According to the directive that has been given to us, this food will be given to the chiefs because they are the people to distribute according to their number, which they know” ; urged the public to stop spreading misinformation and instead rely on credible sources, including local authorities; encouraged anyone with concerns to report them to his office or health officials; said food distribution will continue as planned and called on all eligible families to collect their supplies.

a6274.speaker: United Nations Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF)
a6274.name: United Nations Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF)
a6274.speech: On May 22, said it allocated US$10 million to support life-saving humanitarian assistance for more than 270,000 people in the Upper Nile region.

a6274.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) (statement to Eye Radio)
a6274.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) (statement to Eye Radio)
a6274.speech: Said the funding would target communities in six high-risk counties, including Canal/Pigi, Fangak, Ayod, and Akobo in Jonglei State, and Panyikang and Fashoda in Upper Nile State; said these areas have been severely affected by overlapping crises, leaving families in critical need of immediate humanitarian support; said that since the escalation of conflict in Upper Nile State in March, more than 130,000 people have been displaced, including thousands who have reportedly crossed into Ethiopia.

a6274.speaker: Ms. Gbeho, UN official
a6274.name: Ms. Gbeho
a6274.title: UN official
a6274.speech: Said the CERF funding will help ensure they receive food, cash assistance, seeds, tools, fishing kits, shelter, non-food items, water, sanitation and hygiene supplies, as well as health, nutrition, and protection services.

a6445.speaker: Adam Dawed, General Manager of Amhara Pipe Factory
a6445.name: Adam Dawed
a6445.title: General Manager of Amhara Pipe Factory
a6445.speech: “We encounter a big challenge in the market as our quality greenhouse material price is higher than imported ones.” ; According to the manager, power cutoffs during production incur a high production cost, shortage of foreign currency also makes human resources and machines idle.

a6445.speaker: Adam Dawed, General Manager of Amhara Pipe Factory
a6445.name: Adam Dawed
a6445.title: General Manager of Amhara Pipe Factory
a6445.speech: “We hope that there will be a good market in African countries when the Continental Free Trade Agreement is implemented.”

a6445.speaker: Some research (unspecified, cited)
a6445.name: Some research (unspecified
a6445.title: cited)
a6445.speech: According to some research, producing in the greenhouse film is said to boost productivity by 50 percent and makes all plants grow uniformly.

a6524.speaker: Jenny Comalie, Namcor board chairperson
a6524.name: Jenny Comalie
a6524.title: Namcor board chairperson
a6524.speech: Announcing the official handover of the facility, noted that while construction of the facility, situated in Walvis Bay, commenced in January 2015, the corporation had foresight to recruit and train competent Namibian staff, who, in the process, also assisted the government with the completion and commissioning of the facility.

a6524.speaker: Jenny Comalie, Namcor board chairperson
a6524.name: Jenny Comalie
a6524.title: Namcor board chairperson
a6524.speech: Further indicated the facility will not only be used for Namcor's trading purposes but also to host other international oil marketing companies such as Vitol and Gunvor, Vivo and Total to ensure it is utilised optimally and that Namibia becomes a strategic gateway through which neighbouring African states are supplied.

a6524.speaker: Jenny Comalie, Namcor board chairperson
a6524.name: Jenny Comalie
a6524.title: Namcor board chairperson
a6524.speech: Added that the first shipment of commissioning stock arrived on 1 December 2020, valued at N$407.3 million, which heralded the testing and commissioning of the facility ; “Namcor has already begun to successfully sell the commissioning stock to its retail, commercial, bunkering and export customers, as well as other local marketing companies with success.”

a6524.speaker: Immanuel Mulunga, Namcor managing director
a6524.name: Immanuel Mulunga
a6524.title: Namcor managing director
a6524.speech: Explained commissioning the facility meant bringing in fuel equivalent to the capacity of the terminal to test the operation of the entire system ; assured the nation that the commissioning has so far been a resounding success and that the fuel is safe and clean for use.

a6524.speaker: Immanuel Mulunga, Namcor managing director
a6524.name: Immanuel Mulunga
a6524.title: Namcor managing director
a6524.speech: Stated that even though Namcor owns and operates the massive facility, this does not give them any right to influence fuel and pump prices in Namibia.

a6524.speaker: Immanuel Mulunga, Namcor managing director
a6524.name: Immanuel Mulunga
a6524.title: Namcor managing director
a6524.speech: Said that, according to Namcor's mandate, the corporation looks forward to rolling out more service stations in the coming months in a bid to take services closer to people across the country; explained the target is about 33 service stations to be completed by 2024, and that by end of June this year (2021), eight Namcor service stations, currently under construction, are expected to be operational.

a6529.speaker: Jose Andres, World Central Kitchen founder and chef
a6529.name: Jose Andres
a6529.title: World Central Kitchen founder and chef
a6529.speech: “Today, World Central Kitchen lost several of its sisters and brothers in an Israeli army strike in Gaza.”

a6529.speaker: World Central Kitchen, US-headquartered organisation
a6529.name: World Central Kitchen
a6529.title: US-headquartered organisation
a6529.speech: Called the incident a “tragedy” and reiterated that “humanitarian aid workers and civilians should never be a target” ; said an Israeli strike killed several people delivering food aid to the besieged Gaza Strip on Monday.

a6529.speaker: Health ministry in Gaza (Hamas-run territory)
a6529.name: Health ministry in Gaza (Hamas-run territory)
a6529.speech: Said the bodies of four foreign aid workers and their Palestinian driver were brought to a hospital in the town of Deir el-Balah after an Israeli strike targeted their vehicle, and that four of those killed were foreigners.

a6529.speaker: Hamas
a6529.name: Hamas
a6529.speech: Said the aid workers included “British, Australian and Polish nationalities, with the fourth nationality not known”.

a6529.speaker: Anthony Albanese, Australian Prime Minister
a6529.name: Anthony Albanese
a6529.title: Australian Prime Minister
a6529.speech: Confirmed one of his country's citizens, volunteer Zomi Frankcom, was among those killed.

a6529.speaker: Adrienne Watson, White House National Security Council spokesperson (post on X)
a6529.name: Adrienne Watson
a6529.title: White House National Security Council spokesperson (post on X)
a6529.speech: “We are heartbroken and deeply troubled by the strike that that killed @WCKitchen aid workers in Gaza.” ; “Humanitarian aid workers must be protected as they deliver aid that is desperately needed, and we urge Israel to swiftly investigate what happened.”

a6529.speaker: Israeli military
a6529.name: Israeli military
a6529.speech: Said it was “conducting a thorough review at the highest levels to understand the circumstances of this tragic incident”.

a6529.speaker: United Nations
a6529.name: United Nations
a6529.speech: Issued stark warnings about the dire levels of hunger stalking all 2.4 million Gazans, and has accused Israel of preventing deliveries of humanitarian aid.

a6529.speaker: UN-backed report (19 March)
a6529.name: UN-backed report (19 March)
a6529.speech: Warned that half of Gazans were feeling “catastrophic” hunger and projected imminent famine in the territory's north.

a6529.speaker: International Court of Justice (the world's top court)
a6529.name: International Court of Justice (the world's top court)
a6529.speech: Has ordered Israel to “ensure urgent humanitarian assistance” in Gaza without delay, saying “famine is setting in”.

a6529.speaker: UN agencies and charities
a6529.name: UN agencies and charities
a6529.speech: Warn that ramped-up deliveries by air and sea fall far short of what is desperately needed, with trucks still the most efficient way of delivering aid.

a6529.speaker: Antony Blinken, US Secretary of State
a6529.name: Antony Blinken
a6529.title: US Secretary of State
a6529.speech: Said it was the first time an entire population had been classified at severe levels of “acute” food insecurity.

a6529.speaker: AFP tally of Israeli official figures
a6529.name: AFP tally of Israeli official figures
a6529.speech: Puts the deaths from Hamas's October attack at about 1,160 in Israel, mostly civilians.

a6529.speaker: Hamas-run health ministry in Gaza
a6529.name: Hamas-run health ministry in Gaza
a6529.speech: Says Israel's retaliatory campaign, aimed at destroying Hamas, has killed at least 32,845 people, mostly women and children.

a6529.speaker: Daniel Hagari, Israeli army spokesman
a6529.name: Daniel Hagari
a6529.title: Israeli army spokesman
a6529.speech: “There are more terrorists in the hospital than patients or medical staff”, adding that 900 people had been apprehended at the sprawling Al-Shifa complex, with over 500 of them “definitely” militants.

a6529.speaker: Spokesman for Gaza's civil defence agency
a6529.name: Spokesman for Gaza's civil defence agency
a6529.speech: Said Israeli forces had killed about 300 people in and around the hospital during the two-week operation.

a6529.speaker: Anwar el Jondi, Palestinian
a6529.name: Anwar el Jondi
a6529.title: Palestinian
a6529.speech: “People trapped in Al-Shifa hospital died of hunger. Some drank water from bathroom drains.”

a6529.speaker: Several doctors and civilians at the damaged Al-Shifa complex
a6529.name: Several doctors and civilians at the damaged Al-Shifa complex
a6529.speech: Told AFP that at least 20 bodies had been found, some of which appeared to have been driven over by military vehicles.

a6529.speaker: Israeli military
a6529.name: Israeli military
a6529.speech: Said Monday that 600 soldiers had been killed since the start of the war.

a6529.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a6529.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a6529.title: Israeli Prime Minister
a6529.speech: Vowed to ban broadcasts from Israel by Qatar-based news channel Al Jazeera, after the Israeli Parliament granted him new powers, calling it a “terrorist channel”.

a6529.speaker: Al Jazeera (the broadcaster)
a6529.name: Al Jazeera (the broadcaster)
a6529.speech: Said the Israeli prime minister's comments were a “dangerous, ludicrous lie”.

a6529.speaker: Damascus and Tehran
a6529.name: Damascus and Tehran
a6529.speech: Said there were strikes on Monday in Damascus on the consular annex of Israel's arch-foe Iran.

a6529.speaker: Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, a war monitor based in Britain
a6529.name: Syrian Observatory for Human Rights
a6529.title: a war monitor based in Britain
a6529.speech: Said 11 people were killed in the strike on the Iranian consular annex.

a6529.speaker: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps
a6529.name: Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps
a6529.speech: Said seven members were killed, including two senior officers, Brigadier General Mohammad Reza Zahedi and Brigadier General Mohammad Hadi Haji Rahimi.

a6529.speaker: Israel
a6529.name: Israel
a6529.speech: Did not comment on the strike on the Iranian consular annex in Damascus.

a6529.speaker: Hossein Amir-Abdollahian, Iranian Foreign Minister
a6529.name: Hossein Amir-Abdollahian
a6529.title: Iranian Foreign Minister
a6529.speech: Blamed the United States for the attack: “The Americans must take responsibility”, according to state news agency IRNA.

a6529.speaker: Dmitry Polyansky, Russian representative
a6529.name: Dmitry Polyansky
a6529.title: Russian representative
a6529.speech: Said the UN Security Council will on Tuesday hold a public meeting, requested by Russia, on the strike.

a6546.speaker: Legislative staffer (anonymous)
a6546.name: Legislative staffer (anonymous)
a6546.speech: “If Saah Joseph is genuine about supporting staff welfare, he should advocate for significant increases in salaries and benefits” ; “He joined his colleagues to reduce every benefit of the staffers. Now he wants to offer them US$10,000 and call it a morale-boosting loan? This is not support, it’s a slap in the face.”

a6546.speaker: Stanton Witherspoon, popular media commentator of Spoon Talk
a6546.name: Stanton Witherspoon
a6546.title: popular media commentator of Spoon Talk
a6546.speech: “Senator Saah Joseph is wrong on this issue. He has never shown any track record of fighting for legislative staff or introducing supportive legislation on their behalf. This is concerning and shameful.”

a6546.speaker: Saah H. Joseph, Senator of Montserrado County, Liberia
a6546.name: Saah H. Joseph
a6546.title: Senator of Montserrado County, Liberia
a6546.speech: Speaking at a recent People’s Action Party (PAP) gathering, emphasised the need for democratic governance within political parties and rejected the idea of one-man control: “No one man should control and direct the lives of the people. The people themselves must be in charge and decide their own destiny”; revealed that PAP has already made a US$100,000 down payment on a permanent party headquarters.

a6647.speaker: Willdale (brickmaking company)
a6647.name: Willdale (brickmaking company)
a6647.speech: Says it has set its sights on exporting its products to Mozambique and Zambia to boost its foreign currency generation.

a6647.speaker: Nyasha Matonda, Willdale chief executive
a6647.name: Nyasha Matonda
a6647.title: Willdale chief executive
a6647.speech: Recently told The Financial Gazette that Mozambique will be the starting point for the regional push: "We have had serious inquiries coming through and we have been there..."

a6773.speaker: United States mission in Niger (press statement)
a6773.name: United States mission in Niger (press statement)
a6773.speech: According to a statement from the American mission in Niger released on Monday 3 June 2024, the United States has provided, through USAID, nearly 176 million dollars in additional humanitarian aid for West Africa: "this additional USAID funding, which includes funds from the recently adopted bipartisan supplemental appropriation, will support communities in Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Chad, Mali, Mauritania, Niger and Nigeria facing colossal humanitarian needs as a result of conflict, food insecurity and displacement" ; "these funds will be provided through United Nations partners and NGOs, including the United Nations World Food Programme, UNICEF and the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs" ; the funds will enable "our partners to reach more people with food assistance, nutrition, safe drinking water, emergency health care and protection for the most vulnerable, as well as other essential aid" ; "this funding is more crucial than ever because the humanitarian responses in each of the countries are largely underfunded and needs far exceed the available aid" ; "the United States is a leading donor for the humanitarian response in the Sahel and Lake Chad basin regions."

a6773.speaker: United States (press statement of the American mission in Niger)
a6773.name: United States (press statement of the American mission in Niger)
a6773.speech: The United States calls on other donors to join them in "scaling up aid to this region in order to save lives and alleviate the suffering of the most vulnerable."

a6925.speaker: Lia Tadesse (MD), Ethiopian Minister of Health
a6925.name: Lia Tadesse (MD)
a6925.title: Ethiopian Minister of Health
a6925.speech: Writes that Ethiopia is taking groundbreaking steps in women's health, that the country's contraceptive prevalence rate jumped from eight per cent in 2000 to 41pc in 2019, and that "Our government has increased funding for family planning and focused on expanding access at the community level, employing 42,000 health workers across 18,000 posts, all of which have helped us achieve remarkable progress. But our contraceptive supply has not kept pace with this ever-growing demand." ; Says the Ministry of Health, which provides women like Amina with a range of free contraceptive choices, "faces a country-wide shortage with a significant financing gap for family-planning products," and that women and girls' health is "too often - and too readily - put on the back burner during challenging times, despite the dire consequences of going without contraceptives."

a6925.speaker: Lia Tadesse (MD), Ethiopian Minister of Health
a6925.name: Lia Tadesse (MD)
a6925.title: Ethiopian Minister of Health
a6925.speech: Says of health financing: "We embraced innovative health-financing strategies in Ethiopia to stretch our resources. The goal is to close the financing gap in the short term and to increase country ownership (and thus decrease reliance on donors) in the long term." ; Notes that the Ministries of Health and Finance signed a country compact with the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) to increase domestic financing for family planning, and that a second, complementary structure - a partnership compact signed between the Ethiopian government, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the David & Lucile Packard Foundation, the Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, USAID Ethiopia, and the Netherlands - will see the Ethiopian government triple its contraceptive funding and contribute 11.1 million dollars over three years, to be matched by the donors, filling nearly 70pc of the estimated funding shortfall: "This is the largest investment in family planning that Ethiopia has made in 20 years." ; Concludes that "progress can be made when government agencies work together - as Ethiopia's health and finance ministries did - and engage effectively with donors."

a6925.speaker: Studies (cited)
a6925.name: Studies (cited)
a6925.speech: "Studies have shown that every dollar invested in family planning produces more than eight dollars in socioeconomic returns."

a7215.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7215.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7215.title: President of Ghana
a7215.speech: Expressed gratitude for the High Commissioner’s four-year tenure in Ghana and stated key areas for the ongoing Ghana-United Kingdom cooperation; lauded the High Commissioner for her “positive engagements” throughout her time in Ghana ; He reflected on the long-standing historical relationship between Ghana and the United Kingdom, describing it as having been “so far so good” ; emphasised the mutual need for deeper economic partnerships and trade moving forward and noted the dynamic changes in the global landscape, including the diminishing nature of traditional development assistance and the necessity for developing countries like Ghana to strategically reposition themselves.

a7215.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7215.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7215.title: President of Ghana
a7215.speech: Acknowledging the UK’s significant support in counter-terrorism efforts, he specifically commended cooperation in intelligence gathering and training. “We appreciate the partnership we have shared in the fight against terrorism,” President Mahama stated, adding that “We will continue to rely on the UK for help and cooperation in intelligence gathering and training to prepare ourselves in the event of any attack.”

a7215.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a7215.name: John Dramani Mahama
a7215.title: President of Ghana
a7215.speech: Said that there was progress with strengthening the Cedi, declining inflation and renewed investor confidence in the Ghanaian economy. “I am happy to report that it’s going well,” he said, detailing the first quarter economic performance report. “The first quarter report on economic performance indicates a GDP growth of 5.3 per cent, inflation has reduced from 23 per cent to 18 per cent since January, and we hope to bring it down to 13 per cent by the end of the year, so that should create some relief for Ghanaians in terms of the cost of living and we will continue to maintain fiscal discipline.”

a7215.speaker: Daily Graphic (report)
a7215.name: Daily Graphic (report)
a7215.speech: The report by Daily Graphic quoted President Mahama as saying that there was progress with strengthening the Cedi, declining inflation and renewed investor confidence in the Ghanaian economy.

a7215.speaker: Harriet Thompson, outgoing British High Commissioner to Ghana
a7215.name: Harriet Thompson
a7215.title: outgoing British High Commissioner to Ghana
a7215.speech: Responding, High Commissioner Harriet Thompson, who is leaving Ghana after serving in Ghana for over four years, expressed her gratitude for the warm support and cooperation she received during her tenure. She acknowledged the successful implementation of various British-sponsored interventions during her time.

a7286.speaker: Pentagon officials
a7286.name: Pentagon officials
a7286.speech: Gathered European diplomats and delivered a blunt warning: U.S. security assistance to Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia would be scaled back. The three NATO members on Russia's border, they were told, must prepare to rely less on Washington.

a7286.speaker: David Baker, senior Pentagon official
a7286.name: David Baker
a7286.title: senior Pentagon official
a7286.speech: Drove the point home—under President Donald Trump, the U.S. military would be focusing inward, prioritizing homeland defense.

a7286.speaker: Some European diplomats
a7286.name: Some European diplomats
a7286.speech: Worried the shift would embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin.

a7286.speaker: Estonia (government)
a7286.name: Estonia (government)
a7286.speech: Reported that Russian MiG-31 jets violated its airspace for about 10 minutes before being intercepted by Italian F-35s.

a7286.speaker: Poland (government)
a7286.name: Poland (government)
a7286.speech: Said Russian jets buzzed an oil platform, following recent drone incursions.

a7286.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7286.name: Donald Trump
a7286.title: US President
a7286.speech: After several hours, he warned the Estonia incident could spell “big trouble.” ; Following last week's drone episode in Poland, he had only posted cryptically on Truth Social: “Here we go!”

a7286.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7286.name: Donald Trump
a7286.title: US President
a7286.speech: At one tense call with European leaders, he accused them of expecting the U.S. to “bail them out” while still funding Russia's war machine through oil purchases. Days later, he demanded the EU slap 100% tariffs on China and India for buying Russian oil, calling it a precondition for U.S. action.

a7286.speaker: Aaron David Miller, veteran diplomat and analyst at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
a7286.name: Aaron David Miller
a7286.title: veteran diplomat and analyst at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
a7286.speech: Said Trump may simply have concluded that the conflicts are more intractable than he had hoped. “He's not interested in doing anything unless he sees that the expenditure of effort and political capital will be worth the return,” Miller said.

a7286.speaker: Europe's diplomats
a7286.name: Europe's diplomats
a7286.speech: They warn that a softer U.S. line risks encouraging more aggressive Russian behavior.

a7286.speaker: Alex Plitsas, senior fellow at the Atlantic Council
a7286.name: Alex Plitsas
a7286.title: senior fellow at the Atlantic Council
a7286.speech: “The more America steps back, the more provocative Putin becomes—he senses weakness and division in Europe.”

a7286.speaker: Baltic states
a7286.name: Baltic states
a7286.speech: Pleas from the Baltic states to reverse aid cuts.

a7286.speaker: White House official (anonymous)
a7286.name: White House official (anonymous)
a7286.speech: Insisted: “Many of our European allies are among the world's wealthiest countries. They are fully capable of funding these programs if they choose.”
